It ran under the sofa, under the heating pipes, and my grabber literally fell apart in the process.  Suction cups came off, springy arms disconnected.  It was terrible. reviewText: The colors of the train set are bright and appealing.  The packaging is well thought out in terms of presenting and protecting the product.  But this is definitely a toy train without much attempt to real accuracy.  So the appeal of the item is definitely aimed for children but it doesn't appear to be sufficiently robust to withstand a child's play.  The smoke is pretty noxious and I turned it off immediately.  It would be nice if the lights and the sounds could operate independently because the sound becomes annoying fairly quickly while the lights are still fun (circling the holiday tree in a dimly lit room).  The hooks from the cars to the cars and from the engine to the cars are definitely fragile and the hook from the engine wouldn't be able to be replaced.So this is a mixed review.  Size and colors are very appealing, track is easy to set up, but small hands will probably have problems with starting and stopping the train (small switches on the sides under the engine cab) and hooking the cars to each other and the engine.  It's too childish for adults and too fragile for children.

I bought this to replace a Twelve South Book-Book cover for my iPad Air 2; the Bookbook was a beautiful leather cover, but wasn't functional enough for me to use.  This cover looks very good (very clean/modern) and provided me with a LOT more versatility in a small package.  I use my iPad as a laptop, and had been using Apple's bluetooth keyboard...This case allows me all the functionality I had before with a lot more options.The keyboard lasts for a week for me without needing to charge it, and since I am currently a student, I type into it about 8 hours a day (not sure how long it will last, since I charge it over the weekends).  I like the multiple options for viewing that I have with the iPad in relation to the case; I can quickly flip the iPad over and easily use it as a tablet, while holding it and the keyboard fairly comfortably (when I stand up for work, I like to do this)...I can keep the iPad tucked into the tray on the keyboard and use this as a traditional laptop, actually keeping it on my lap for quick typing (similar to the micro-laptops popular a few years ago), and when I finally get to my desk, I extend the metal brace out from the case and can adjust the viewing angle so I am not hunched over.  When I get home, I quickly detach my iPad from the case with the "camera lens-cap" (that's exactly what it appears to be) that attaches the iPad to the arm, and can use my iPad for reading and watching movies.I am impressed with the fit and finish of the device.  It looks good, and since I am a middle-aged guy in a professional school, I appreciate the fact I don't look like I went too cheap on my device.  The keys are definitely smaller than a full sized keyboard, but I was quickly able to adapt to them and can touch type on the device without issues.  I've actually written a few papers on it when I cannot get access to a regular computer, and didn't have any real problems.As far as a case to protect the iPad, I appreciate the rubber strap that closes the keyboard over the iPad like a clamshell; the addition of the small rubber pads around the keyboard ensure nothing touches the glass of my iPad, and I think I have about the same protection as I would have gotten with a rigid case.All things considered, this case saved me from buying the new "super iPad" with a keyboard, and allows me to work alongside guys with laptops or Surface Pro tablets without having any loss of function.

reviewText: I ordered this item last December, and it was.... well, a little less great than I had hoped. Overall, New Trent has made some very necessary changes to the design, which have truly improved this case.I also want to highlight the fact that this company takes feedback so seriously, and that they made changes based on feedback. This kind of responsive service isn't the norm out there, and I think it's important to bring that up. This case is now a much better offering, and you can't really go wrong with it. The only thing to keep in mind that it is really a two handed affair to set it up, and it isn't the lightest keyboard case out there.I would now feel good about recommending it, especially with the very strong customer service ethic that this company has.

The Airbender 2.0 keyboard case is a good keyboard and case for the iPad Air.  The keyboard can  attach and detach from the case itself and function separately.  This is accomplished by squeezing a clip on the back that secures itself like a camera lens.The case itself is a standard protective hard plastic case.  All the ports are available and easy to access.  It's slim and lightweight.  You can expect standard protection from a short fall.  There is no front protection however.The keyboard is comfortable.  You have to charge it with a standard usb cable included. Once charged, you turn it on or off with a flip of a switch.  You only need to pair it to your device once with a push of a button.  Once your device finds the Bluetooth signal, you enter in a numeric code on the keyboard and your set.  The keyboard also pairs with other tablets and phones quite easily.  The keys can't match a real desktop keyboard; it's plastic and you feel it.  But it gives a nice tactile feeling.You don't even need the case and keyboard to be connected, but if you do, you can adjust the angles by pulling the silver colored "stand" out.  With the stand in, the angle of the iPad isn't the most comfortable view however.  Once you tilt the iPad backwards for a better angle, the weight topples the whole thing backwards.  Pulling the stand out fixes this and is pretty much needed every time.  Minor hassle.  The tilt tension on the stand feels pretty solid.  You can also pull the whole stand out and use it to independently prop up your iPad.It's most useful for typing, most likely for searches, comments, emails if you're using a tablet or phone.  Other buttons like brightness, volume control, are handy.  Laptops are always going to be the best for mobile work, but if not, professional journalists, ebloggers, or any profession that uses email would benefit from this product with an iPad Air.I would have liked a lighted keyboard in terms of improvement.

I already had a similar case (the Aerb brand), so I can compare the two directly.New Trent superior on the following points:- The rotation is butter-smooth, even right out of the box. I don't quite understand the 60-degree position lock, but it's no biggie. Just a little strange since I can't imagine what I'd use that kind of iPad position for.- The metal stand adjustment is very smooth as well. I had no trouble taking out the iPad stand and putting it back into the keyboard. I can see this being important when I'm traveling and have to use it at weird angles.- Buttons are more robust.- The case stays closed with the little rubber lock strap. The Aerb doesn't have that, but it has a similar magnetic lock/unlock so there have been times when I've run down the iPad's battery because it was stored upright and case was cracked open.- The automatic Bluetooth reconnection is very nice as well. When I don't want to drain the keyboard's battery and turn it off, I can simply turn the Bluetooth back on and it will reconnect. Nice touch!- The backspace key is where it usually is on a regular keyboard. For the Aerb case, the "Lock iPad" key is where the backspace key usually is, and I've locked my iPad a billion times by accident, when I wanted to delete something.Aerb superior on the following points:- The existence of a "Delete" key. For the Aerb case, you can delete by using the function key with the lock key, but I tried that with the New Trent and it didn't work. It's a small thing, but I'd like that.- "Right where I left it" screen unlocking from the keyboard. With the Aerb, if I accidentally press the lock key, I can press it again within a few seconds and the screen will be back exactly to what it was without having to slide right to unlock. On the New Trent, when I have accidentally pressed the lock key, when I press it again to turn the screen back on, I have to unlock the iPad manually from the screen.Clearly, New Trent wins! From just the smoother swivel and the locking case, I'd take it over the Aerb. It's got a better price, to boot!The ruggedness of the New Trent case will have to be determined as I use it more. The Aerb looked pretty rugged, but pieces of the plastic started breaking off in the corners after 4 months of use, and I hadn't been carrying it around that often. At first glance, the New Trent seems tougher because it is hard plastic and not soft plastic, but time will tell!

Upon screwing on the antenna and following the setup instructions scrupulously, it worked from the get-go. Excellent bandwidth, no slow-down through DOCSIS 3.0 35Mb/s service (two users) compared to CAT5 Ethernet hard-wired connection to router. Screw on the antenna SMA connector firmly but carefully, and if possible, plug it into a USB port (v2.0 minimum) near the top of the cabinet of the desktop PC where it can have a clear 360 view. See photo. Plugging it into a rear-panel USB port and orienting the antenna vertically, right against the metal chassis of the computer, is a poor RF configuration. If you must plug it into the back of the PC, angle the antenna out about 45 and make sure the back of the PC has direct line-of-sight to the wireless gateway/router. Sure, it will "work" no matter where or how you plug it inbut what you won't know is how much it BETTER it could work with a really strong signal in both directions. The stronger the signal, the higher bandwidth that can be maintained.

I am a huge incense fan; I find that certain scents are great for setting the mood for meditation or relaxation after a particularly long day at work. I also like using incense to make my home smell nice when I am going to have company over. I have tried frankincense and myrrh incense scents separately, but never together so I was definitely intrigued by these incense sticks by Plant Guru.The incense comes packaged nicely in a resealable bag; the bag has an easy-to-read label for easy scent identification. The bundle is huge compared to most other brands of incense that I have tried. While most brands only give you about 20 incense sticks, Plant Guru includes approximately 185 grams or 85-100 sticks in each bundle. My particular bundle included 86 sticks which is plenty of incense for quite some time. The scent is exactly what youd expect a mixture of frankincense and myrrh to smell like; a beautiful blend of the piney, lemony, sweet and woody aroma of frankincense and the earthy aroma of myrrh. I find that these incense sticks are quite strong; not a bad quality in my opinion as that means that instead of burning 2 or 3 sticks at once like I do with my other incense brands, I only have to burn one stick to fill my living space with this lovely scent. Each stick is approximately 10.5 inches long and the burn time is quite good for the size. I have burned about 8 of these sticks and they have all burned for at least 40 or so minutes; a tiny bit shorter than the advertised burn time, but considering thats about average for incense sticks and you get a whole lot more than you do in any other package Ive tried I didnt really mind that a whole lot. As far as setting a nice mood for meditation; these certainly get the job done. These incense sticks are charcoal based so they do have a black soot-type coating which can go all over the place so you do need to be careful not to rub your hands on your face or clothing before washing your hands. Overall, I am quite impressed with the quality and burn time of these incense sticks and can definitely see them being a great little gift for the incense lover in anyones life.

Without the VacuVin a bottle of wine presentings a daunting undertaking - are we ready to drink 4-5 glass of wine right now? The VacuVin eliminates this problem by allowing you to remove the air from the bottle after you  have opened it, which slows the oxidation which turns the wine sour.You  stick the rubber stopper snuggly into the bottle top, place the VacuVin on  top and pump its handle 4-8 times (depending on how empty the bottle is).  With each pump, the VacuVin sucks out more air though a narrow slit in the  rubber stopper. You can feel the vacuum inside building as each pump takes  more effort. The vacuum then holds the slit closed.The beauty of this,  is that it takes no time at all - maybe 15 seconds, tops. With the VacuVin,  I've been able to enjoy the same bottle of wine for upwards of a week. One  hint for a better vacuum seal, is to run the rubber stopper under water  before using it - a little moisture helps achieve a better seal, especially  when the rubber stoppers are no longer new.

reviewText: Video gaming has come a long way since the late 1970s and early 1980s.  Game budgets have balloned into astronomical proportions and marketing campaigns have become blitzkrieg extravaganas.  Major video game titles, like the major "tent pole" movies of the summer Hollywood so heavily relies upon, represent significant investment of capital.  If you believe the marketing copy, each of these big budget video games represent the very best the video game industry has to offer. *Sadly, such hyperbole is very seldom the case, especially with non-Nintendo titles.  Unlike Nintendo's IPs, which are consistently recognized as some of the most enthralling, well-designed games out there, and also certainly among the most bankable, newer games must establish such a strong, realised world and marketing presence that big budgets are in demand.  While Nintendo and Mario/Link are the family friendly alternatives, there exists an large opening for more adult oriented fare to enter and dominate the market place.  Enter Rockstar and the GTA titles which, while always controversail, has long helped bring adult themed video gaming into the mainstream with writing that is both brilliant and deeply satirical of modern day life..GTA V follows the Grand Theft Auto social commentary satire the series is so famous for, and expands it tremendously, becoming a mirror of America after the economic downturn. Rockstar paraodies everything form Facebook to political classes to celeberity culture, etc.  The use of smart phones in our culture is also heavily featured.  GTA has become the video game equiliant to South Park - there is no sacred cow left standing by the end of Rockstar's commentary on America.CHARACTERS:  Rockstar changes up the GTA formula by introducing three main protagonists.  GTA V features Michael, a retired, bored middle-aged criminal who reminds me of Henry Hill's fate at the end of "Good Fellas"; Franklin, a young gang-banger reminsent of Carl Johnson, and Trevor, a psychotic, in-your-face nutjob who is so unhinged that you can't help but feel he is little more than a caricature than an actual person.  Of the three characters, Trevor is by far the most over-the top.  At any time (other than specific points restricted for story purposes) you are able to switch between the three characters, which are at differing locations depending on time of day.  The game will then take you to where the characters happen to be at the time. Each location fits into the character's story and place in the GTA universe.One of the weak points with the GTA series has always been the sometimes unavoidable narrative inconsistencies brought on by its open-ended gameplay, all the while moving the characters down specific narrative arcs.  Likewise, the Elder Scrolls games from Bethesda suffer from this flaw to some extent.  By introducing three characters, Rockstar is able to marry that illusion of cohesion between character and gameplay much better than the superficial unions of past games.STORY: Rather than gradually introduce a wide cast of supporting characters and develop their backstory, Rockstar has streamlined the writing, focusing largely on Trevor, Franklin, and Michael, at the expense of having numerous, secondary characters that so frequently stole the show in previous titles.  That's not to say there aren't any memorable secondary characters; rather, the narrative focuses on the big three (and I don't mean Harry, Ron, and Hermione) and delves expensively into their lives and how the characters' fates become inextricably intertwined as the game proceeds.SETTING:  After the sprawling landmass of GTA: SAN ANDREAS, which featured three cities divided by expansive countryside, deserts with secret government bases that may or may not hold alien bodies, and rural communities that appear to be straight out of Deliverance, GTA IV focused on a reimagined New York City.  GTA V returns to the west coast, taking place in Los Santos, one of the three cities first introduced in SAN ANDREAS.  While not as widely broad and disconnected as "San Andreas", GTA V features the series' biggest map yet, which also includes surrounding mountainsides and Sandy Shores, a costal village. Unlike previous titles, the entirety of Los Santos and the surrounding areas is available from the very beginning.  The gaming world, while always artificial, feels truly alive.GAMEPLAY:  The gameplay elements of GTA IV have all been finely tuned.  AI is superb,.  You can engage in a wide variety of activities, such as base jumping, cycling, flying, golfing, hunting, tennis, triathalons, vehicular racing, and yoga. Expanding on "Vice City", "San Andreas" and "GTA IV", you can also unlock vehicle storage facilities and purchases businesses and go on missions to help those businesses make profit.  You can even play the stock market on your smart phone.  There are also individual activities tailored to specific characters (Michael visitng a therapist and playing tennis or practicing yoga, Trevor hunting, etc).Like any GTA game, there is driving, and a LOT of it.  For a series focused so heavily on driving, GTA V is the first time that Rockstar has nailed the driving down so effectively.  Cars handle so much better overall (though the joy rides can still turn into some memorable crashes).  Certain elements of driving in past titles have been frustrating, due to how wildly odd they handle.  vehicles handle with precision, while still providing a wide variety of gaming experiences.  Unfortunaly the flying sequences are still dreadfully awkward to control  Another great addition is if you fail missions, you are no longer required to repeat the driving segments of those missions.MISSIONS:  The shining point of GTA V, undoubtedly, is the missions, which constitutes the core of the gameplay.  Several of the missions are tailor made to one of the three characters.  Michael's missions deal with his increasingly fragmented family life as he goes back into crime.  Franklin becomes more and more involved with grand theft auto and assassinations.  Trevor's missions intimately suit his extremely psychotic psyche with larger-than-life explosions and wild, freewheelin' rampages that would earn anyone in real life a one way ticket to an impenetrable mental instution.GTA V grades missions on different qualifiers, contingent upon completing optional objects as well as time, appealing to the speedrunners out there.  The biggest addition (and it's been a LONG TIME COMING), is, after failing a mission three times, you are able to skip that section of the mission, though your score will be directly effected.  Since the 1996 N64 classic "Super Mario 64", open world games have been notorious for having that one, infuriating mission.  In the GTA series, often times that mission must be passed in order to progress, and it's high time Rockstar has come up with a solution for those "one mission" nightmares that so often send us into tirades (I'm looking at you, "Wrong Side of the Tracks" from "San Andreas"!).  Why develop all these hours of content if, because of one mission early in the game, the player eventually puts down your product, with the game unfinished?  Likewise, you can replay missions at any time, another needed addition to the franchise.A major addition is the heist missions, which involve all three characters.  Rockstar is able to show off just how effective they are at featuring three protagonists in the Heists missions, and add a new depth of gameplay not previously seen in the GTA universe.  The heists can be done one of two ways: guns blazing, ala Clint Eastwood, or channel your inner Solid Snake and infiltrate and plunder by stealth.  Depending on what route you go, the three protagonists then must chose a crew (such as computer hackers, drivers, gunmen, etc) with varying degrees of experience.  The better the crew, the more expense, but the less likely the mission will fail or you will run into further complications.  The multiple character mode, the choice between stealth and combat, the action-packed setpieces, along with the variables of the crew you have chosen, make the heists some of the most engrossing missions ever seen in an open world game.  Unfortunately there is only a handful of such missions in the game.  The future of GTA, and sandbox games in general, resides in these type missions, and theres so much untapped potential in them that it almost comes off as a criminal waste.  Off the beaten path you will find a wide variety of one-off missions that are both fun and imaginative.VISUALS: Fantastic and breathtaking.  The game features a wide variety of environments for Rockstar to show off their graphical prowess, from scuba-diving sequences to cross-country to wealthy neighborhoods to seedy, dank areas more terrifying than they are amusing.  The variety of locals is astonishing and adds to the overall texture of the game.  You will be very hard-pressed to find a more gorgeously looking game on the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3, with all the details becoming much more crisp and the character animations superb.SOUND:  Fantastic as always.  GTA V does everything the other games in the series does and more, with a wider variety of musical content, new original music, and the best talk radio (featuring the GTA III perennial favorite Lazlo) this side of Rush Limbaugh.  The voice acting is top-notch, as always.CRITICISM:  The game comes across as rather misogynistic, with no strong female characters treated with respect, even given the criminal nature of the gameplay. Sometimes Frankenstien's seams show through, breaking the illusion of reality, and the scripting becomes apparent.  While boundary-pushing content has always been a hallmark of the game, there is an (unskippable) torture mission that Trevor must complete that is little more than a veild criticism on the US policy of waterboarding.  Even for a game as intentionally lewd and morally reprehensible as GTA V, this mission is deeply troubling and the one time that Rockstar breaks the illusion of "this is just a video game" and actually feeling dirty about yourself as a human being, even though you are playing as Trevor.ENDING COMMENTS:  The GTA games have become a massive cultural phenomena the likes of which few games can attest too, attracting both controversy and fanatical players.  With the release of GTA III in 2001, Rockstar introduced a fantastically realised, open sandbox world which was deeply satirical in nature and have only built on the foundations laid by that groundbreaking game.But twelve years in the electronic entertainment industry and pop culture in general can be an eternity.  With the prevelanace of increasingly violent and sexual content regularly displayed throughout our culture, games like GTA V aren't quite as shocking as they were in 2001, let alone 1994 with Mortal Kombat's spine-ripping fatalities went all the way to the United States Congress.  Even Christine Hefner, Hugh Hefner's daughter, has stated pornography has become such mainstream that it can hardly qualify as edgy anymore.  By this point, the major groundbreaking gameplay elements introduced in GTA III has become a matter of course for big-budget titles.  To Rockstar's credit, they have prefected and honed the GTA gameplay to such fine precision that GTA V stands proudly as among the best games ever made in the admittedly very young medium of video gaming history.Overall, despite the jaded, cynical culture we now live in, GTA V pushes the boundaries of sex, drugs, and violence to a new level.  Like Insane Clown Possy's Dark Carnival mythology , I believe Rockstar is more moral than their detractors allow for.  They hold up a twisted, exaggerated picture of life in America today, twisted by crime and sleaze which is enacted by deeply pathological, flawed people. reviewText: This is a good, functional tripod.  Here's what I like and a couple things to know prior to making your buying decision:1.  Flexible "octopus" arms work great.  They bend/pivot well and have an adequate number of closely spaced joints to bend around anything you come across that you want to use as a picture shooting surface.  There is also sufficient tension at these joints to keep them in place once you set them where you want them.  This is key in making the unit functional.2.  The ball joint that connects the legs to the phone holder is a little stiff.  It functions to pivot the phone where you want but you need to grab very close to this joint and be mindful about how you want it to move so you don't mess up the octopus leg placement.3.  The quick release phone housing works get.  Make sure to remove this part when you're attaching the phone cradle for the first time.  This is the only way to really tighten that connection well.  I didn't realize this at first and it made for a really wobbly join here.4.  The phone cradle itself is not the easiest thing to use.  The tension is good and it holds your phone in place well but there isn't really a great place to grab and open the unit when your phone is in place (when you're trying to remove the phone).  It just makes it a little bit awkward since your primary focus is protecting your phone which leaves one hand to manage the housing unless you use the phone as a lever to pull one side open.  I just don't like to do that to my phone so it makes it hard.5.  The phone housing is EXACTLY large enough to hold my Samsung Note 3 and Note 4 WITHOUT their cases.  It can not accommodate the phones when they are in their cases.  Kind of annoying to have to remove them in order to use the tripod.  Smaller phones than mine probably won't have this issue. By my measurements, the internal opening is 3 1/8" wide.6.  The remote was easy to pair with my phone using bluetooth.  The remote works well.All in all, I'm happy with the purchase because it offers me a good tool to use on vacation and in the field when working.I received a discount on this item in exchange for my honest review.  I hope the pictures/comments/videos are helpful to you.

The witches have dire predictions for Kate and Atlanta, she worries about becoming evil, but even with war on the horizon and the threat of her father looming larger than ever, she's not going to let anything ruin her wedding.SPOILERS AHEAD:I actually waffled on how many stars to give this book. Some of it felt contrived and rushed to me and I thought it had a weird tone with strange pacing and plotting. It starts out with a bang but then shifts into a different gear and suddenly we're visiting with every character ever and catching up and talking about wedding plans and babies as if the witches didn't just predict that everyone was going to die. It's definitely ushering in the end of the series (hopefully paving the way for Julie and Derek) and tying off loose ends and stuff, so maybe this is why it had such strange pacing and plotting?The whole thing with Jim warning Curran not to marry Kate (he believes she's using mind control on Curran) bothered me.  Jim's never been that great of a friend to her (imo) but seriously, what kind of "friend" warns your fiance that you're manipulating him? That's pretty messed up.Then we've got Derek accusing Kate of making Julie her slave.  Apparently, the Derek in this book has forgotten all about the fact that Kate swapped blood with Julie TO SAVE HER LIFE, and he's conveniently ignoring the fact that Kate's always gone out of her way to avoid giving Julie orders even on accident because he accuses Kate of creating slaves left and right.  And i can't even blame him (or at least I don't think I'm supposed to). You see Kate's gettin some strange urges and suddenly struggling not to become like her father (not like her at all). There are extenuating circumstances (the magic) but apparently Kate is not allowed to have faults; she must be a paragon of virtue and altruism if she doesn't want to turn into her father.When Kate lets her magic loose and Curran worries she's become her father, he doubts her instantly, and that's not like him at all either (whatever happened to him accepting her for who she is?).  Even before this, he and Barabas take her to task for losing her temper (which was pretty understandable given the situation). Like Kate says at one point, she's bled for this city and saved it over and over again and she's never asked for anything in return but now everyone instantly doubts her and apparently, they're all right to do so because this contrived plot line calls for it (funny how Curran can--and often does act like a tyrant and it's considered cute but when Kate supposedly acts like one it means she's turning into her powermad father and has to be stopped).What's weird about this whole Kate-struggling-not-to-turn-into-her-dad thing is it just sort of went away mid-book (*poof* just disappears), because later on Kate goes to the Casino and lets her magic loose and everyone's suddenly encouraging her to use her magic to persuade people to do her bidding.  Weird. It all seemed a bit contrived and rushed to me.  Don't even get me started on Adora, a brand new character who undergoes years of character development in like, the span of a page (she is able to overcome a lifetime of brainwashing after one lecture from Nick!), not to mention how Kate suddenly decided Curran was dumping her because she didnt tell him about Adora.On the plus side, there's some great stuff in here: Christopher's past is finally revealed and then there's Kate's grandmother and Era who are both founts of information (i freaking LOVE Era and hope she sticks around), and we see the factions all coming together (though again, it seemed so rushed--i wanted more development!).  I also loved Roman's role in this book (i think it's so cool he officiated!), and I enjoyed the battle at the end so I gave it 3 stars.

reviewText: If you enjoy a stronger, fuller cup of coffee and want to extract more flavor from your coffee beans, this is the unit. Is produces a brew that is somewhere between a French Press and espresso. It may use more coffee grinds but the flavor is very rich. If you use the inverted method, the flavor is even more pronounced, regardless of the bean type. When you are in a hurry, filling the unit and pushing the hot water through without allowing for brew time will still produce a better tasting cup of coffee than the paper filter or automatic drip coffee makers. For more than one cup, you'll have to make each cup separately, not great when you're having company. One remedy, add more grinds to the Aeropress for a stronger brew and then dilute the result to taste with hot water.Clean-up is a cinch, an easy quick rinse. Using a steel mesh filter saves on the paper filter restocking and allows for more of the oils to pass through, increasing flavor. Regarding the paper filters, I use mine 15-20 times each before discarding them. They work just fine and each filter lasts a long time. Aeropress can make hotel coffee packets taste a lot better but you'll be better off bringing your own more finely ground coffee on the road with you.This is the best coffee maker available and the price is ridiculously low considering the quality of the brew. Get one.

reviewText: Despite having played around with a variety of entry-level gear directed at coffee fanatics, I somehow did not come across the Aeropress until very recently.  My brother-in-law, who shares a passion for experimenting with all things coffee, mentioned it to me a number of times, but I was left with a mental image of a large, unwieldy contraption that was basically a glorified French Press.  Actually, the Aeropress is much easier to clean than a French Press, and produces a (mostly) clean cup that has more in common with a pour-over or Chemex.You'd be forgiven for looking at the product picture of the Aeropress and still having no clue what's going on, so I'll try to describe it in basic terms.  Basically, the Aeropress consists of two plastic tubes with one fitting snugly inside the other and guided by a rubber gasket.  There is a grate in the bottom of the narrower tube, and this locks into place.  On top of that, you place either a paper disposable filter (it comes with 100) or a reusable mesh one.  As with most metal filters, the latter option is convenient and eco-friendly, but may let through a bit more particulates.Where the Aeropress differs from French Press is that you are using air pressure to force the water through the grounds, out of the filter, and into a coffee cup below.  French Press still allows the grounds to continue steeping in water, almost like tea, but this can result in a lot of bitterness (in my opinion).  The grounds are compressed into a dry cake that you can literally push off of the rubber gasket once you are done.  You may wish to rinse off some of the other parts to clean up, but you almost don't need to - there's little clean up to do after discarding the grounds and the paper filter.PROS - The Aeropress is very small, durable, and portable, and it makes a great cup of coffee.  The early cups I made were very clean and without much bitterness.  Moreover, I've heard (and I suspect) that it's a more forgiving method of brewing coffee than something like Chemex, where variations in water temperature and ground size really seem to throw things off.  I've read reviews of people who take these to hotel, heat water up in a microwave or hotel coffee maker, and then have cafe-quality coffee ready within minutes.  There are also iOS apps populated by online communities of Aeropress fanatics, group-sourcing different brewing techniques and measurements with this simple, affordable brewing device.CONS - I don't have anything really negative to say about the Aeropress thus far (hence the 5-star review), though I do wonder if its advantages over a simple pour-over funnel are a bit overstated.  You can buy a plastic or ceramic pour-over cone and several hundred filters for about $15.  Assuming you have good water and a proper grind with quality beans, I've gotten results with pour-over that are about as good as you could hope for using any method.  And cleanup for pour-over involves nothing more than tossing the filter with the grounds in it and splashing some water in the funnel.That being said, the Aeropress sort of acts as its own measuring device, as it includes a scoop for measuring grounds and has numbers marked on the tube to guide how much water you should pour in.  It's arguably one of the best ways to make a consistently high-quality single cup of coffee.UPDATE (12/14/16): Posting again only a week or so after purchasing the AeroPress because I absolutely love it, and might not have captured my full enthusiasm for it in the original review!  I think the key thing to appreciate to about the AeroPress (alongside its small size, convenience, and ease of cleanup) is how remarkably forgiving it is as a brewing technique.  By comparison, something like a Chemex pour-over is capable of stunning results, but is also very sensitive to changes in grind size and proper measurements.  I appreciated this after purchasing a burr grinder for the first time and realizing that my ability to control grind size more accurately was leading to better and more consistent results.  But with the AeroPress, I'm not using a scale, and I'm almost positive my coffee measurements (done in "scoops") and water amounts (measured by "shots" marked on the cylinder) are frequently off by a bit.  (Sometimes more than a bit, if I'm hurrying).  It doesn't seem to matter.  Aeropress can make stronger cups or weaker cups of coffee, but it's very hard to make a "bad" cup of coffee, at least compared to other popular methods.  If it breaks, I'm re-buying it.  I may end up owning more than one anyway.

reviewText: We have an expensive DeLonghi espresso maker.  I prefer (by far!) the coffee that comes from this simple machine.  I don't know if it's from the filtering out of the fine particulates or from the trapping of the oils on the filter paper, but the result is a less bitter cup of coffee with a much smoother taste.Incidentally, I have a different technique for using the Aeropress.  I start with the unit inverted, plunger down.  I add the coffee and hot water, stir it up, then put on the filter paper and perforated lid.  I flip the whole thing over and press the coffee into the mug.  Doing it this way insures that all the water/coffee mixture stays in the cylinder for the desired amount of time.  If you follow the instructions, coffee starts to drip through immediately and a substantial percentage has run through by the time you've finished stirring and inserted the plunger.Highly Recommended!

Let me start by stating that I'm a wine freak. I collect and consume lots and lots of wine, including many bottles that have spent years and years cellaring, resulting in very fragile corks that are all too eager to crumble. Moreover, I suffer from severe arthritis, making it difficult for me to open bottles. As a result, over the years, I've accumulated a vast collection of corkscrews, ranging from fancy machinery to simple waiter's models. My all-time favorite was the WineMaster by VaccuVin, a piece of genius engineering with a bunch of gears ensuring that the cork comes out with no effort at all. Alas, they are very fragile--I've broken quite a few--and VaccuVin discontinued them a while ago (they sell for a fortune on eBay).Since breaking my last WineMaster a couple of years ago, I've been on an obsessive quest to find the perfect corkscrew, buying every possible type, from the priciest machines to the simplest, from all over the world. To be frank, I've never heard of HiCoup, so this particular corkscrew was never on my radar. One day, one of my decanters fell and shattered, so I went online to replace it. I came across a similar model by HiCoup at a fraction of the price, so decided to go for it. As I was about to check out, I noticed a promotion offering this corkscrew for free. Needless to say, I had little hope that this simple cheapo corkscrew would be the end of my quest...I was wrong. This is the greatest little corkscrew ever made! The downfall of the vast majority of waiter's corkscrews is poor balance, which causes the screw to exert more pressure on one side of the cork than the other, easily damaging an old, crumbly cork. This is perfectly balanced and fits my hand like a glove. The 2-stage boot (like Coutale, but much better) locks onto the bottle and the cork slides out with imperceptible effort. The perfect alignment prevents even the most fragile corks from crumbling. (Alas, some corks completely disintegrate over the years, but that what the Monopol Butler's Friend is made for.) Thank you HiCoup for making the perfect corkscrew and then giving it away for free! I can't recommend this corkscrew enough! BRAVO!!!

It's super easy to use and maintain.I love the "Bold" brew setting. Adds a unique flavor to my coffee. It takes a little bit longer to brew on that setting but worth it. The timer function works fine and the clock keeps its time so you don't have to worry about it changing unless it gets unplugged.Cleaning is pretty easy. Just need some distilled white vinegar and you run it through the system and let it sit for 30 mins then rinse with a few cycles. You're supposed to do that once a month on each side. The filter baskets come out and can be hand washed. I hand wash the pot but I think its dish washer safe. The top opens up for easy access and can even be pulled apart and snapped back together. The mug it comes with is useless to me so I threw it away pretty quickly.The single serving side does not use K-Cups. I use a paper filter I fold the right way to act like your typical drip coffee maker. I love the auto stop when removing the pot to pour a cup while the coffee is still brewing. This works by a spring and a gasket that closes when you remove the pot and opens when the pot is in place. I did however forget to put the top of the pot back on after cleaning once so this gasket was closed while it was brewing and it over flowed and grinds got everywhere. This was a pain to clean but I haven't done it again.I'm very clumsy and have hit the pot against things and dropped it with out any cracks or chips so it's built well.There are a few negatives but nothing that ruins the coffee maker for me, but for the review I'll go over them.-The power cord is a little short. I think it's about 3 feet long so if you don't have an outlet near where you will put the coffee maker you'll need an extension cord.-The mug is useless. It can easily spill and doesn't keep the coffee hot for much longer than a regular ceramic mug.-You can't use the single serve and the pot side at the same time. Switching from one side to the other turns off the other side.-The coffee pot is glass with a plastic brim. Fluid gets caught up on this brim so you'll never get the last little bit of coffee.-The reusable filter on the single serving side wasn't very good. I instead would use a regular paper filter folded the right way.-If you are going to use a regular mug in the single serving side it splashes quite a bit. To prevent that, the base comes apart and you can stack up the pieces to raise the cup closer to the drip so there is less splash and less space for it to escape the cup. Depending on the mug it can become a scary balancing act. I try to use a tall mug instead of the balancing act when I can.These little issues are worth it for the quality of the cup of coffee the machine brews. I would buy again whenever this finally gives out on me.

I'm very happy with the 2015 version of the Roku 2.  It is easy to use, the performance is very snappy, the menus are fluid and the menu system and navigation is so intuitive that most people will never need a manual or any tech support.Setup is also easy:  connect it to your HDTV or home theater receiver using an HDMI cable (not included, but you can one cheap on Amazon), plug in the power adapter, and follow the on-screen instructions.  It's so easy, my parents could do it.  As with Blu Ray players, the HDMI cable carries both the video and audio signals.  The Roku's picture and sound quality are very good on my modest system (though, like all other streaming boxes, picture and sound from internet streaming are not quite up to par with the best Blu Ray discs).The included remote is nicely designed and is much easier to use than the remotes that came with my TV and Blu Ray players.  However, as an "IR" type remote, it requires a direct line of sight to the Roku box, so you can't hide the Roku box in a cabinet, it has to be out in the open.  The Roku 2 comes with Duracell batteries for the remote, which should last for years.  (The batteries that came with my last Roku box in 2011 lasted until 2014.)If you have an iPhone or Android phone, you can use your phone as a remote using a free app from Roku.  Doing this can come in handy.  If you want to enter text using the Roku remote, for example to search for a movie or to set up your Netflix account, you have to move the cursor to each letter and select it; this is a bit tedious.  Using the smartphone app, you can pull up an on-screen keyboard and type text in directly; it's quicker and easier.  Also, the latest version of the Roku smartphone app has voice search:  just say the name of the movie you want, and it will show you all the channels that has that movie, then touch the one you want and it'll take you right there.  If you misplace your Roku remote or the batteries die and you don't have replacements handy, it's nice to be able to use your phone as the remote.  And lastly, you don't need a direct line of sight to control your Roku box with the smartphone app, because the app uses your wifi network rather than infrared.The alternatives to Roku are Amazon Fire TV and Apple TV.  All three platforms have their advantages and disadvantages. Apple TV is the only one you can use to view content from the iTunes store, and it can also mirror content from your iPhone or iPad if you have one.  But the Apple TV hasn't been updated in years and is overdue for a new version (hence its recent price drop).  Amazon Fire TV is great if you have a Kindle Fire tablet; Amazon Fire TV also has voice search which works great for searching for content available from Amazon.  Roku has the most channels of all of them and is my favorite.  But all three platforms have their loyal fans.If you choose the Roku platform, you can buy this Roku 2 or the Roku 3 for $30 more.  The 2015 versions of the Roku 2 and Roku 3 offer identical performance; the only difference is the remote:  The remote that comes with the Roku 3 has an earphone jack, a motion sensor for playing games on the Roku, and a mic for voice search.  For me, these extra features are not worth the extra $30.  But they will be for some people.If you have an older Roku (I did), the 2015 updated Roku 2 will be a big step up in performance.  It's really easy and fast to use, and navigating the menus is super easy and intuitive.  If you've never used a streaming box, the Roku platform is a really excellent one, almost no learning curve and well designed with just about everything you could want from a streaming box.One last caution:  The Roku 2 and 3 were originally introduced 2 years ago.  These 2015 updated versions are very good, especially the 2015 Roku 2.  But this is not a fundamentally new device.  Roku is likely to come out with a "Roku 4" later this year that will offer 4K resolution, faster performance, and probably some other new features.  If you don't have a 4K TV, the 2015 Roku 2 is a really great option.The other reviewer has a less favorable perspective and you should read his/her review before spending your hard-earned money.  But my experience with the new Roku 2 is very positive and I recommend it highly.

reviewText: OK...so I bought this (along with a leather cleaner) for my leather couch which wasn't looking the best and needed something. It took some getting used to using especially on a big old couch - but I picked it up and I let it sit expecting to come back later and wipe the excess off -- within one hour the couch had soaked it up...and it looked and felt so much better.  I cannot undo the damage we already did but not using a higher grade product -- but this wills save us from the future.  I'd only suggest taking time to do this -- it's not easy to work with - but you will get the hang of it and you will be pleased with it. I received the Whisk & Ladle 21 Day Portion Control Diet Containers. These containers are color coded and are an effective but simple way to plan your meals. The lids of the containers are conveniently labeled with the food group that belongs inside them. These containers are made with a high quality, food-grade plastic that is safe, economical and BPA + DEHP free. They are microwave, dishwasher, and freezer safe.These are great portion control containers. You get 7 containers all a different color and for a different food group, except the seeds and dressing container, it has 2 of those containers. So the green container is 1 cup and is for vegetables. The red container is 3/4 cup and is for proteins. The yellow container is for carbs and is 1/2 cup. The purple container is for fruits and is 1 cup. The blue container is for fats and is 1/3 cup. The two orange containers is for seeds and dressings and is 2 tablespoons. These containers come with a nice brochure that shows you how to calculate your calorie level and what foods are considered vegetables, fats, fruits, carbs, etc. I ran them through the dishwasher and had some peas left over from dinner, so I ended up putting them in the green container before looking at the brochure. Which if I did look , I would have known I should have used the yellow container for carbs. The container seals good and the lid did not pop off or leak when I turned it upside down. I do recommend these portion control containers from Whisk & Ladle.

reviewText: Is an electric toothbrush better than a standard one? In some situations definitely. An electric toothbrush can cover a larger area faster, so you clean more surfaces in the same amount of time. Brushing by hand is much slower and requires more attention to detail. Some studies have shown people who use an electric brush had less plaque and gum disease. They are particularly useful for kids because they often think that an electric toothbrush is more fun and easier to use, which in turn, encourages them to use it more. My teenage son also found an electric toothbrush much more effective while wearing braces as it did a better job of cleaning in and around the metal parts. Dentists often recommend electric toothbrushes if they find youre not removing enough plaque with a manual toothbrush.The main drawback to an electric toothbrush is the cost. Regular toothbrushes usually cost a few dollars, while you can spend nearly a hundred dollars or more on an electric one. Brush heads for power brushes need to be replaced as often as manual ones, too. The extra expense can add up. This toothbrush is comparatively inexpensive and six replacement heads run around $10. That's a very reasonable investment that may save you money at the dentist in the long run.

I would like to thank Midori Spring for sending me a sample of this product to test and review.The tea arrived in a small 30g tin. Opening it for the first time, I was amazed by the vibrant green colour of the powder and the earthy aroma exuded by this product.Well, this was my first ever experience with having to prepare green tea which isn't in a teabag so I was a bit nervous. I put a little less than half a teaspoon in a mug. I added about half a mug of hot (about 70C, not boiling) water and whisked the solution until foam formed on the service. I then added a little bit more water to dilute it further.The taste of this green tea shows its class. It has nothing to do with the traditional teabags we usually buy. To say that it has an enjoyable flavour would be a lie. The first sip didn't go down well at all and I found myself wincing from the strong bitter taste in my mouth. I was actually about to throw it down the sink, but I persevered, not wanting to waste a product claimed to have such health benefits. Then I remembered that I can add some honey to make it taste more sweet and that did the trick. The tea became more bearable and slightly more enjoyable.To date I have tried it another three times, each time changing something. I reduced the amount of tea to a quarter of a teaspoon and I tried sugar instead of honey. The amount of water added to the mixture is crucial. One has to find the right balance and mixture which gives the best possible experience.This green tea is of superior quality, but it can never replace my regular teas and coffees. However, keeping in mind its beneficial properties, I have included it as part of my diet taking a cup on a regular basis. If you're a regular green tea drinker, you do well to try the Midori Spring Green tea Matcha.

One was a Radio Shack 5 element FM antenna (about 5' long) and a UHF antenna (about 3' long) mounted on a 15' pole on top of the house making the antennas at apx 30' up in the air. So if correct, I should be able to remove the two large antennas and replace it with the RCA ANT751, Compact Outdoor HDTV antenna.Guess what? I was correct! It works perfectly; now one antenna does the work of two and I get all the HDTV channels even from Mexico, about 20 miles away.  Also all of the local HDTV channels about 15 miles away. And the classical music FM station in Tecate, MX about 30 miles away.  It is extremely easy to assemble and mount on an outside pole.The antenna is a sweet performer, its light and not very big. I should mention that I live in what is called a good radio area b/c the house is clear and the land falls off gently in all directions. It is NOT that its HIGH up but has a CLEAR shot in any direction.  And as with any antenna, the HIGHER up they are, the better they perform.

I was immediately dissapointed at the omnidirectional aspect of this unit when I read that it works best when laying flat rather than upright...but if it functions as advertised, then it would not matter what position it was in. Just go to this link and punch in your zip code:  http://transition.fcc.gov/mb/engineering/dtvmaps/  Secondly, mount the antenna high enough that it is not blocked, in the short distance, by trees or anything else. Product is professionally packaged and sealed.If 2013 was the year of the alphabet cream (BB, CC, and their ilk), then the 2014 Asian import of choice has got to be the konjac sponge. Wondering what the hell a konjac sponge is? Well, stay tuned, because we're about to rock your world. .Made from the root of the konjac plant, these squishy sponges are used in your cleansing routine to help you more effectively dislodge, dirt, oil, and blackheads. "Konjac sponges are made from a natural fiber that absorbs a lot of water, so it has a very unique texture, kind of like a thick piece of rubbery felt," explains Dr. Jessica Wu, a Los Angeles dermatologist and author of Feed Your Face. "It has more texture than a dish sponge, but it's softer than a loofah and has a finer texture than a washcloth, so it's safe to use on your face. Your skin will feel very soft and smooth, and makeup will go on better."While Americans are loyal users of washcloths, the concept of using a sponge to cleanse is a little hard for some to accept. But, once you get over the "I'm washing my face like I wash my dishes" vibe, you'll find yourself hooked on this weird little squisher. "Because of its bouncy, rubbery texture, it makes a rich lather using less cleanser than you'd normally need with a washcloth," says Dr. Wu. "It dries quickly in between uses to prevent bacteria or mold from building up in it, whereas a washcloth might stay damp in between uses." And, since you replace them monthly, there's no danger of using a dirty, moldy germ-infested sponge on your visage.Dr. Wu says she recommends konjac cleansing for anyone with acne or clogged pores because the fibers help unclog those plugged pores in a way that a washcloth or just your hands can't. She also likes it for those with sun-damaged skin because it can help gently slough off those dull, dry flakes. If you're a hardcore SPF wearer, konjacs can also remove those stubborn, water-resistant sunscreens that won't come off with cleanser alone.Ready to add one to your routine, but not sure exactly how to do it? Dr. Wu has you covered: The first step is to soak your sponge in warm water for at least five minutes. "Konjac sponges are very hard when they are dry, so you must wait until it softens so you don't injure your skin," she warns. Splash your face with warm water, then squeeze a few drops of cleanser directly onto the sponge, says Dr. Wu. Massage the sponge in circular motions, concentrating on those areas that have blackheads or dry patches.You want to maintain a rich foaming lather while you are massaging, notes Dr. Wu, so add more cleanser if your lather is looking weak. She cautions to avoid those areas with healing pimples, infections (like cold sores), or abrasions and be sure not to press too hard or you could scratch your skin.Once you've finished cleansing, rinse the sponge with warm water, squeeze out the excess water, and let your sponge air dry. Dr. Wu likes daily usage, but do what feels best for your skin  if daily makes your skin feel too raw, drop down to two or three time a week. If you are using a retinoid or other medicated cream, Dr. Wu says it's in your best interest to check with your derm first before trying this out. I've tried a few different protein powders, so I feel I have a base of comparison.  I would say this is not my favorite for sure, but it's also not the worst.  For what I have been used to (whey), yes, this has a much different taste and a much different texture.  But it has more than just whey (it doesn't have whey at all in it).  The spirulina gives it a bit of a cooling/earthy sort of flavor to it, but after the first few sips/bites, I don't mind it at all.I've made it a few times now.  The first time I mixed it up just as the instructions say, and again, it wasn't bad at all after the first sip and your tastebuds acclimate.  The vanilla flavor is pretty good, and does a decent job of coming through over the other flavors.  The subsequent times I've had it, I've made it into more of a smoothie - adding unsweetened cashew milk, lots of ice cubes (like 15 or so), and various flavors (one time, I used peanut flour + cocoa powder; another time, a few drops of cherry extract plus some frozen cherries).The texture is admittedly different from what I am used to - whey protein whips up so smoothly in my Vitamix and tastes smooth and creamy.  This was *not* lumpy or anything like that - it blends up great - but the mouth feel is a bit gritty/grainy? I think it's just the nature of the brown rice protein - but it's definitely not clumpy or lumpy or anything like that.My one real complaint/suggestion is when I opened the bag, the "reasealable" Zipploc was extremely hard to re-close - would take me way too long and I wouldn't be sure if I sealed it properly.  So my easy fix was to just pour the contents of the bag into a large container with the included scoop and then fold the bag and put it in a baggie with the container so I can refer back to it if I need to.This really does fill you up, especially when made into a smoothie.  I've had a time where I made it after already having something else to eat and I could only eat a little less than half of it because it filled me up so much.So, all in all, I would recommend trying it - especially if you can find a sample size to try out.  If you are sensitive to whey or just want a vegan formula, this is very good one to try.  It's one of my current favorite among the vegan powders I've tried. I personally like the taste of the whey powders better, but not everyone can consume whey, and that's the glorious thing about there being many different ones out there - something to suite everyone!*I did receive a discount on this item, but I review items honestly regardless of the price I pay for it. If I don't like something about an item, I will say so because as a customer I want to know the good, the bad, and the ugly of any product I am considering purchasing.

reviewText: I'm a fan of NOW Foods essential oils in general.  I think they tend to be a fair price for a good, reliable quality product.  Over the years, I've had only one "suspect" oil from NOW, and was able to get a quick, satisfactory solution to my problem.Eucalyptus oil is undoubtedly one of the essential oils I use the most, particularly in the winter to help combat colds and congestion.  The large, 16 oz container of oil doesn't have a dropper included, which makes sense to me because essential oils degrade plastic (quite rapidly, too!).  It takes me a looong time to get through the whole bottle, and I've no doubt that if I kept a dropper lid on the bottle, it'd be rendered useless before the oil was depleted.  The mouth of the bottle is large enough for my 1/4 and 1/2 tsp measuring spoons to fit easily, so I use those to keep spills to a minimum when I'm mixing my little blends.As far as usage goes, I'm leery of using most essential oils undiluted on my skin.  Almond, avocado or any light vegetable oil works well to carry the eucalyptus for topical use.  For aromatherapy I like a blend of about 4 parts Eucalyptus, 2-3 parts Lavender and 1 part Peppermint in a diffuser (or on the stove in a pot with water) during the winter to help with congestion.  Some other reviewers have complained about the potency of the oil they received.  I've been very satisfied with what I've received, but I suppose perception of scent is somewhat subjective.  This oil doesn't have the knock-your-socks-off harshness associated with some eucalyptus-scented products (like Vapor-eze), but I find it more pleasant and no less effective for being less sharp.Finally, if you're looking for ideas and instructions about using essential oils, rarely will you find details on the bottles of oil themselves.  There are a lot of safety considerations (for example, asthmatics, pregnant women, and those with sensitive skin should use caution, depending on the oil) and lots of options for personalization in blends.  I suggest Dodt's The Essential Oils Book: Creating Personal Blends for Mind & Body for a beginner's guide or The Aromatherapy Bible: The Definitive Guide to Using Essential Oils for more in-depth knowledge.

reviewText: I have a pretty large kitty (15-16 lbs, and he is very tall/ long) , so I had always used an open large litter box, because all the covered ones I had seen in pet stores weren't large enough for my cat.  However the odor from when he took a poo always bothered me because it lingered into my bedroom right when I was trying to relax (not a pleasant smell lol).  So after a lot of searching and reading of reviews I decided to get this "jumbo" one, the size advertised attracted my attention.  Upon receiving the package I opened and inspected it, it was brand new, very nice, without any damage, stickers and upc code still attached.  I did immediately notice that the size is not what was advertised (22x20x18 assembled and 22x17x18 inside the unit), the inside of the box is quite a few inches smaller, especially the "floor", because of the angle and way it is constructed.  My old open litter box was actually 22x18, and although this hooded one seems large from the outside, it actually has less usable space inside and on bottom/ floor.  So I put them side by side to see if my cat would like it, and sure enough he went inside and used it within 30 minutes, he actually fit inside.  I left them side by side for about 4 days until he got used to the new one, then I took away the old open one.  It has been about 30 days now and my cat uses it without any problems, there is 80% less smell from the poo, and about 70% less messy litter scatter around the box.  The clear swing door is removable in case kitty doesn't like the door.  I haven't had any sort of leaks from the seams on the sides, I noticed some people experienced that.  Overall I am satisfied, I deducted 1 star because the size advertised is misleading.  I would recommend the product.ADDITION TO PREVIOUS REVIEW:It's been a while now, about a year, and the box is holding up very well, my cat uses it without problems.  Still love it, still highly recommend it!PS i ended up taking off the "swinging door" simply because i think my cat prefers it without the door.

So far so good!Arrived on time and setup was easy.Just roll it out, plug it in, and fire it up!I've owned and slept in a variety of airbeds in my time, ranging from glorified pool floats, to high-dollar name brand units.The one thing that is true about all of them is that they will eventually leak. And per Murphys Law, this always happens in the middle of the night, on a day when you really need to sleep, or when you have important guests over, etc. Some beds last longer than others, but eventually they will all leak.The part that sold me about this bed was the "Never Flat" pump. If it performs as-advertised, it will eliminate or greatly the reduce the one biggest problem that faces every single airbed eventually, leakage...The bed itself appear to be very sturdy. Its a nice deep design so it can be placed directly on the floor and still be easy to get in and out of. The material feels thick enough, and the seams are flat and cleanly bonded. I would expect this bed to go at least the normal duration before it starts to leak (a couple of years of occasional use, or 4-6 months of constant use).But what (should) really set this bed apart it how it performs after it starts leaking. Even if the bed springs a leak, one that would normally put you on the hard floor in a matter of hours, the pump will kick in to re-inflate it and keep you reasonably comfortable for the rest of the night, or the rest of the week, until you can find some time to patch it.Originally I thought this meant the primary (loud) pump would kick on for a few seconds to get it back to full, which would have been enough to wake me up, but would still be preferable to having to switch it on and off manually, or reinflate with a hand-pump like the old days.But to my surprise when I got this set up, the "never flat" pump is actually a separate unit from the normal noisy pump, and it really is almost completely silent! If you're laying right up next to it, and you're listening closely, you can hear it, but it wouldn't wake you up from a sound sleep. And if you lay with your head on the other end of the bed, I bet you wouldn't even notice it at all.I tested it by manually deflating it, and waiting for the never flat pump to kick in. And sure enough it did, and brought the bed back to firm in a couple of minutes.  Its not as fast as the main pump, but assuming its a small leak and it only has to re-pump 1-2 times during the night, it should work perfectly.I also tested the adjustable firmness control. I'm not convinced that the primary pump is controlled by these settings (plush feels just like firm if you let the pump run in auto mode), but when you engage the never flat, and deflate the bed back to where you like it, the silent pump will respond to the firmness control very well. If you set it to plush it will stop early, and if you move it to medium, or firm, the silent pump starts up again to get you to the right setting.Overall its a high-quality airbed to rival the competing products ranging from $50-$300, but with its one "killer-app," the never flat pump, this could easily make this bed stay usable for 2-3 times the lifespan of the other beds on the market.For the price, (and assuming the pumps and seals hold up) its a great deal.

It is a completely neutral oil so that the fragrance of any essential oil added to it isn't changed at all. A little bit goes a long way which makes this oil very cost effective. I purchased this charger to try and simplify the mess of cords and devices that I routinely charge at my desk (4 devices regularly). In my particular case, that meant securing the charger to the underside of my desk using some adhesive strips and then running the cables down the back of my desk. Overall, I was impressed!Disclaimer: I did receive a discount code for the product, but this review is comprised of my own honest opinions about it. I am evaluating this product with respect to its current price, not the discounted price.APPEARANCE: The white plastic is a matte finish, which gives the charger a robust feel. There is certainly some heft to it, and it doesn't feel as though it's been cheaply produced, despite its relatively low price.PERFORMANCE: I tested all USB ports with various devices and got the power levels that Lumsing claims in their description. I don't currently own a QC 2.0 device, but I can confirm (with a Friend's device) that the QC 2.0 port works as advertised. The other ports are listed as "smart" (similar to some other brands sold here on Amazon), and from my testing, they do actively regulate the current through each port depending on your device. My Moto 360 smartwatch drew much less current than my Nexus 5X, as I expected. Overall, performance is reliable and exactly as advertised.PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: The charger comes with a relatively long cord (about 1.5 m, or 5 feet), and two velcro straps. This gave me plenty of length to place the charger where I needed, but that depends largely upon your desk setup. As stated earlier, the rough finish and chamfered edges make this charger aesthetically pleasing, but I still preferred to hide it under my desk for a clean setup.OTHER NOTES: The USB ports are VERY stiff, as others have stated. This is great if you're going to keep cables plugged in constantly, but if you're going to be constantly removing cables, I'd worry about the pressure this charger puts on your cables. On the plus side, the connections feel secure.CONS: My only disappointment with this charger is that it contains soon-to-be-outdated technology. The lack of USB-C ports or even QC 3.0 ports may mean you want to look elsewhere if you're trying to future-proof your charging setup.FINAL VERDICT: Even at full retail price, this charger is a great deal that will simplify your charging experience. It truly does feel like a quality product, and I'm glad to have so many ports available for all my devices. I'm looking forward to using this charger for a long time - but if you're looking for the latest technology, you may want to look elsewhere.
reviewTitle: A great charger from a new brand - but not revolutionary.

Oliver is back and this time, he's spending time with crockery, sharks and giant ants! Yay!On the first story, it was New Year's Eve and Oliver was having fun with the cooking utensils. They magically came alive and talked and danced and cooked! My sons thought these stuffs really happened at night when everyone else was asleep. He'd love to see our own crockery sway and dance at night, much like how Oliver enjoyed their company, too!For the second story, it was a bit frightening to see a shark following Joey, Jumpy's son while they're on the beach. Good thing, Oliver and Jumpy came to the rescue! Whew!And the last one was my kids' favorite, when Oliver went to a magical place where he shrunk in size and was almost eaten alive by beetles. Yikes!Werner Stejskal, as always, bring out the best in my kids' faces. Their huge smile from ear to ear always make me happy after they read an interesting story. They always look forward to Oliver and Jumpy's magical tales and adventures. The illustrations are a delight to see, too! Not only was this an interesting read, it was also educational and informative - two factors why I love reading this series!

NOTE: The author informed me that this book was available at the time for free on Amazon and asked me to write a review.Werner Stejskal continues his series of children's picture books detailing the adventures of Oliver, a cat, and Jumpy, a kangaroo. This is the second volume in the series that I've had the opportunity to read, and it's pretty much the same quality and style as the first, which leads me to believe that if you like one of Stejskal's books, you'll probably like the rest. And, with very young readers, continuity is important. They do better with what's familiar than with radically new concepts from book to book.For those who haven't read any of Stejskal's previous books, Oliver is an "elegant" cat, primarily because he wears a bow tie and a top hat, and Jumpy is a kangaroo (Stejskal is from Australia). The book contains three stories, each of which is composed of several brightly illustrated panels in landscape mode with a sentence or two of written text at the bottom. The illustrations take up about 80-90% of the space on each screen. The first and third stories are 11 panels each (including the title panel), while the second story is nine panels long.The stories in "Oliver and Jumpy" are all fairly basic. In "Crockery Party," a house's pots, pans, and silverware come alive to make a meal for Oliver, Jumpy, and friends. "Shark Frenzy" has the most developed storyline, with Oliver, Jumpy, and her son Joey going off in a boat to play with whales and instead encountering a hungry shark. In "Small World," Oliver magically transforms himself to the size on an insect to get a better look at the world beneath our feet. Although the second story features a shark attack of sorts, it's drawn so that it's not really all that scary, and the shark resembles Charlie the Tuna from the old Star Kist commercials.Without a doubt, the drawings are the best part of Stejskal's book. The first and third story were illustrated by the same artist, Mario Tereso, while the second story was illustrated by Maycee Ann Reyes. I preferred Tereso's work, which is brighter with more different colors, resembling an old Technicolor cartoon. "Crockery Party" is especially entertaining, since each individual piece of dinnerware has its own face, with oversized eyes and a wide variety of smiles and grins. I'm well past the target demographic age for this book, but I really enjoyed the pictures in this story. The pictures in "Shark Frenzy" are more subdued, with a lot of pastels, which does serve as a calming influence in the story.My only real criticism of Stejskal's work is with some of the text. In the earlier volume I read, I thought Stejskal used too many words beyond the comprehension level of his target audience. For the most part, the text in the current book is simpler and easier to read, but there are some spelling and grammatical mistakes that definitely should have been avoided, such as using the misspelled word "poiseness" instead of "poisonous." Later in that story, Stejskal writes "we reached the queen's chamber who just laid an egg." Obviously, it's the queen, not the chamber that laid the egg. While copy editing is important for all books, I think it's vital that authors of children's stories avoid giving them bad examples.I remain quite impressed with the Oliver and Jumpy series. The quality of the illustration is often amazing. One panel in the last story has dozens of individual, colorfully drawn ants, and the overall color scheme in Tereso's stories is often dazzling. The stories are simple but serviceable, getting Oliver and his friends from one panel to the next reasonably well. Plus, the artwork is entertaining enough on its own to invite repeat readings. For families with children who still enjoy picture books, "Oliver and Jumpy" will be a pleasant addition to the library.

reviewText: Amazon's vine program regularly offers me this type of vaguely healthy, vaguely sugary snacks.  Sometimes I accept.  Usually, I am disappointed.  These things, though, are actually pretty good.  They are described as dark chocolate, nuts, and sea salt.  That's pretty much what you taste.  The strongest flavor components are the nuts, which are very lightly salted with sea salt.  So, you taste the nuts, not the salt.  On top of that, they use dark chocolate, but in relatively small quantities so that the nuts remain the primary flavor component.  The fact that they use dark chocolate keeps the bars from being too sweet, and the light amount of sea salt is just enough for the nuts without overpowering anything.  I hate healthy snacks that try to mimic candy bars.  Such attempts generally use poor quality chocolate in large quantities, and usually wind up with about as many calories per gram as normal candy bars anyway.  These bars, though, just taste like what they are.  If you want a snickers bar with fewer calories, you are out of luck.  However, if you like nuts that are very lightly salted, dark chocolate, and don't want something as sweet as a candy bar, these are actually pretty good.

Works fine.  The product should contain a package insert which gives information about the limits of pulse oximetry and directions for using the product and changing the batteries.  Purchasers should be aware that pulse oximeters do not directly measure the oxygen saturation but calculates it.  The calculation is based on the assumption that the hemoglobin is within normal range.  If a user's hemoglobin is low due to anemia for any reason or high (for example because of residing in a location of very high altitude for a lengthy time) then the oxygen saturation number shown in the LED display will be erroneous.  The heart rate number may also be wrong due to low blood pressure or poor peripheral perfusion.  False measurements usually do not indicate a defect in the equipment but a problem with the health of the user.  Professional users of this equipment are trained to manually palpate the pulse while using the pulse oximeter.and then compare this number with the heart rate  shown in the LED display.  If the numbers are in close alignment the measurement is considered reliable.  If there is a large deviation between the two numbers the data shown in the LED display is unreliable and the procedure should be repeated using a differen digit.

First, I don't think I would recommend dosing CoQ10 if you're still young or you're capable of getting it from your diet. However, CoQ10 is very important to your body, so you do want to make sure your body is producing enough of it. Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) is a substance similar to a vitamin. It is found in every cell of the body. Your body makes CoQ10, and your cells use it to produce energy your body needs for cell growth and maintenance. It also functions as an antioxidant, which protects the body from damage caused by harmful molecules. CoQ10 is naturally present in small amounts in a wide variety of foods, but levels are particularly high in organ meats such as heart, liver, and kidney, as well as beef, soy oil, sardines, mackerel, and peanuts.Personally, I worry that I don't eat enough of any of these items, so at my age I dose 200 mg of CoQ10 a day.Coenzymes help enzymes work to digest food and perform other body processes, and they help protect the heart and skeletal muscles. So what are the health claims of CoQ10? Many claims are made about CoQ10. It is said to help heart failure, as well as cancer, muscular dystrophy, and periodontal disease. It is also said to boost energy and speed recovery from exercise. Some people take it to help reduce the effects certain medicines can have on the heart, muscles, and other organs.I could go into details about the positives, negatives, etc of the claims, but it is best you do this yourself.I have been taking CoQ10 for a year now and I can't tell you if I have extra energy, as I've found that the only thing that really helps with my energy levels is exercise, a healthy diet, and a consistent sleep routine. Regardless, I do think this is a very important supplement to my diet.As for this product I did receive a discount for a fair and honest review, but I WOULD NOT put my health at risk, so if it didn't clear my hurdles I wouldn't have accepted the offer. This hurdle is cleared. I love that this product DOES NOT contain silcon dioxide, which is rare these days. The other ingredient that is typical for this type of product is Microcrystalline Cellulose, which is ubiquitous in our foods and supplements.Again, this product does not have it. Now these two ingredients are NOT deal breakers for me, but I do like that this product does not have either.I suggest you do your own research!!!!! And decide if you need CoQ10 and if so how much you need.
