This steam mop really lives up to the claims.  It gets my floor very clean, and when left sitting on hard stains for a bit, brings them up with no problems. Holding it sideways for a couple minutes seems to also help clear up this problem.I'm really psyched about having NO chemicals on my floor, and NO sticky residue. I found that after a few uses they are harder to get the bottom covered, so you have to be careful not to scratch your floor.  If you're not marathon cleaning this isn't a problem though. I read reviews of hard surface floor cleaners on many sites before purchasing the Eureka.  I am very pleased with the performance of this steamer.  I have a linoleum floor in my kitchen and hardwood floors in many other rooms.  When you weigh it against mopping with a bucket of water and sponge mop, I think it has several advantages.  Firstly, the steam.  It takes off tacky pieces effortlessly after just holding the steamer over the area for 5-10 seconds.  Even with my old mop that had a scrub brush on the reverse side for such tasks, sometimes I needed to still get down on my hands and knees to remove them.  The steamer does it with out bending over.  The steamer is not heavy, but has enuf weight to it that you don't need to scrub back and forth over the same area.  In fact, moving slowing section by section is the best way to a clean floor.  At first, I felt like the task was slower, but when you consider that the floor is dry almost instantly, you aren't waiting 20 minutes for the floor to dry before you can walk on it (which is big with 3 kids who are constantly around).  I have even found it relaxing since you aren't bending over pushing the mop back and forth and wringing it out constantly.  It also gets right up to my baseboards.  When using the steamer on my hardwood floors, I move the steamer along quicker so the drying is instantaneous.  Overall, I believe my floors are cleaner with less work!!  The only reason I did not give it 5 stars is that I had anticipated it maneuvering much like my swiffer to get around the toilet.  It does move and twist rather easily, but the bottom of the steamer seems a little big to get in the tighest spot around the toilet.  That's my only complaint, but not much of one when one swipe of a clorox wipe can take care of that area.

I'll start out by saying that we have two large and hairy dogs and that when they come into the house, it's directly into the kitchen, no luxurious mud room, etc.  Luckily we have a porcelain tile floor, and it's a great color.  But still, who wants to feel that grit under your feet?This mop does an adequate job.  I vacuum the floor first to get up the doggy debris and then use the mop.  As many other reviewers have said, the steam lasts long enough for a "normal sized" kitchen.  Ours is not large, and there's usually enough steam to hit parts of the dining room, too.  It's 70 year old oak, so I don't let the steamer sit in one spot, just go over it lightly, and it does a nice job.I like the fact that this mop doesn't use any chemicals.  The hot steam is enough to get up any dried food spills that are on the floor.  Still, I've always used vinegar & water, and I'm missing that sense of clean, so sometimes I spritz the floor first and then use the steam mop.  That gives the vinegar action w/o it going through the steamer, since the directions say not to use vinegar.  Another tip--wet the cloth before you attach it to the steamer.  Otherwise you use up too much steam just getting it thoroughly wet.  I've tried this a couple of times now, and I like the results.  As to washing and drying the cloths, I do put them right in the washer and dryer and they have not shrunk.  They're very sturdy so should last a long time.Why only 4 stars?  I like the steamer.  It's easy to use and does get up a lot of the dirt.  But it doesn't get the floor spotlessly clean.  After I wash it, if I wipe a spot with a clean paper towel, the towel will still look kind of dirty.  Nothing's as good as being on your hands and knees and really washing the floor. reviewText: As a way to keep my flashlight handy and protect it when not in use, this holster has proven versatile. After running a thorough scientific test on Swig Savvy's 17oz Stainless Steel Bottle and determining that it was every bit as good as the name-brand that cost 4x as much, I was definitely interested in trying out one of their larger offerings.  I was curious if it would live up to its claims of keep drinks cold for 24 hours.  The short answer is yes.  More details below.I put 15 ice cubes in the bottle, and filled it the rest of the way with cold water.  Starting temperature of the ice water: 44 F.  I then set it outside in the southern heat for almost 48 hours, to see how it would deal with the temperature.  I tried to measure the temperature in fairly evenly-spaced increments, but life got in the way, so I did the best I could.I placed the bottle outside at 10 PM, when the temperature was 84.Water temp: 4410 AM the next day (12 hours in, 75 outside temperature):Water temp: 45.1(The high temperature reached 94 that day. The bottle was in both the sun & the shade during the day.)Midnight (26 hours in, 78 outside temperature):Water temp: 57.210 AM the following day (36 hours in, 74 outside temperature):Water temp: 605 PM on day 3 (43 hours in, 87 outside temperature):Water temp: 64As you can see, this bottle definitely keeps cold stuff cold for at least 24 hours.  In the first 12 hours, the temperature of the water only went up 1.  It went up ~11 more over the next 12 hours, when it was sitting in 90+ degree heat.  Even 43 hours in, it had only gone up 20 degrees.  The cold water from my sink is 72, so 64 is definitely still colder than that.  For comparison, a plain old cup of ice water that I set outside was the same temperature as the air in about 2 hours.So yes, it definitely does work.  It would probably work even better if the lid was more insulated.  Like some other reviewers, I only got one lid (the plastic sports lid).  While the rest of the bottle stayed completely dry, it did sweat quite a bit during the experiment, which means it was the weak point where heat was able to transfer.  I would guess that the metal lid would be better insulated & provide better performance.  I'm contacting the manufacturer to get the other lid, and will update with their response.  (UPDATE: I contacted the manufacturer, and got a response with the tracking number for my new lid in less than 20 minutes.  That's ridiculously fast service.  Very impressive.)Other than that, no complaints at all.  It's well-made, attractive, and (a true rarity these days) actually exceeds the manufacturer's claims.  5 star product for sure.

reviewText: This product has worked flawlessly. My home has three temperature zones that were hard to manage; basement first floor (Kitchen, dinning room living room), second floor (three bedrooms and hall). I purchased two additional external sensors in addition to the one included with the programmable thermostat. My home's sensor placement is one in the basement, one in the master bedroom and one in the coldest bedroom above a large garage. The programmable thermostat which also functions as a sensor is centrally located on the first floor. The Ecobee3 has modulated the central air  and furnace functions to maintain a very consistent temperature through out my 1800sq. ft. home. It has alleviated much the drastic felt temp differences when moving one level of the house to another. The user interface and programing was not hard and I was able to monitor my energy usage recently from Japan. Great purchase.

I ordered two of these thermostats after doing extensive homework and being very patient. I started looking at the Nest when it first came out but it always troubled me that it had no remote sensors which meant the motion detecting features and temps in other areas would be lacking. The Ecobee3 seemed to be the answer to this dilemma, but still I was patient. The announcement of Apple HomeKit also intrigued me and I had a sneaking suspicion that there might be some integration down the road. My patience bore fruit, but more on that later. The thermostat is fantastic and the added sensors really makes it super functional. I bought two.  One for each of my HVAC systems in a two story home of 3715 square feet. San Antonio moves to within a quarter mile of the sun in the summer, so my units get an Olympic workout in their ability to cool my home. Of the two units I bought, one had a defective display in that it had horizontal white lines across the bottom half inch. I consulted withe Ecobee and they asked me to return the unit to Amazon for replacement. In typical Amazon fashion, they got me a replacement in two days and I sent back the defective unit. The replacement worked as it should. Since getting them a month ago, I have noted my home is very comfortable, more so than in the past, though the energy savings are still out for consideration as I am doing detailed analysis comparing consumption vs cooling degree days. One of the features I a most pleased with is being able to use AC over cool to lower the humidity. This was a huge benefit I really didn't anticipate. Our old thermostats didn't track humidity and simply stopped the system when the temp was satisfied. Setting my desired humidity max at 64% got my home rid of the moisture and I have noticed a marked increase in comfort. Even our tortilla chips don't get soggy nor does my bread get moldy. We sleep way more comfortably. I have also noticed (using the HomeIQ feature) that the thermostats have intelligently learned to turn on the fan to redistribute air to achieve desired temps before turning on the condensing unit. It does this in a way no ordinary thermostat could do. I could go on and on about features. The important thing is that there are more features in store as they refine the firmware. The disappointment? HomeKit hasn't lived up to its potential. I believe Apple bears the blame for this, though I also believe the potential will be fulfilled. At this point, all HomeKit does is allow you to interrogate Siri about your Ecobee3's. Pretty lame. And for some unknown reason (to me anyway), using HomeKit disables the ability of the to automatically decide if I needs to be in heat or cool mode. Go figure. And to share the HomeKit abilities with others I had to load the Insteon+ app and add users in that. Still I give it five stars because there is NOTHING out there like this and the potential is incredible. Very happy with my purchase and I hope they keep at it.

reviewText: I chose to go with the ecobee3 over Nest due to the availability of the remote sensors, future integration with Google Home, and I like the interface much more than the Nest.  My experience from the get go was quite positive. Getting the ecobee mounted and running was pretty effortless, and the nice little stickers they provide to label the existing wires was a nice touch.  I had it up and running in about 15 minutes.The interface to me is very nice and I love using a touch screen vs. the pseudo-analog style of the Nest rotating panel.  The remote sensors are great to allowing me to keep my upstairs cooler at night when we sleep, and not making the thermostat reliant on the downstairs location.  I really enjoy all the customization I can make as well: schedules, sensor activity, alerts, and so on.Overall, the ecobee is a great product and well worth the money.  I have had ZERO issues with it in the past few months I've had it, and once I get my basement finished, I will be adding another sensor to the system so I have 3 total zones controlling and regulating temperature.

It's a little bit smart, but the "smart" home-away is limited: There is no way to set which comfort setting it uses for "home" or "away", for example. You can only use the preset home and away profiles. You cannot change whether smart home/away works at the preset "sleep" time. If you create different comfort presets, then smart home-away function no longer works for them (it's inactive the same as "sleep"). Also, there's no option to set how long it waits for motion before deciding you are away.So, for simple basic setups, this works fine. Temperature seems to quite accurate. I like the outdoor weather display, also.But I've been disappointed by the lack of customization and flexibility with the programming. To me, it feels like lazy product development. This could be a fantastic piece of equipment. There are so many possibilities for this device besides just working as a thermostat (the motion sensors could activate other equipment or lights). It should be possible to customize the schedule (you could set different target temperatures for different sensors, or different motion requirements for home/away at different sensors, or what if it's been smart away all day - it will just switch the heating on at night because smart away no longer functions, etc), but they are just shut down by the poor user interface implementation. Maybe they'll come out with an update. Or maybe Nest will do it first. Overall, I'm disappointed so far.

Ecobee has built on previous smart thermostat ideas with a killer feature: remote sensors.  I have been interested in getting into the smart thermostat world for a few years now but until the Ecobee3 I didn't quite feel the technology was "there".  My previous top consideration, the Nest, was cool but had one major downside: If you spent too much time away from the thermostat, it would switch to "Away" and stop conditioning your house.  Nest realized this shortcoming and released $100 combo smoke detectors and presence sensors.  While I appreciate their thought, $100 per additional sensor is just not realistic for your typical consumer.Along comes the Ecobee3.  In the package you get the Thermostat and a second motion+temperature sensor, and can add more sensors than you'd ever need by buying additional packs (The sensors are about $40 each or so, but are cheaper if you get a bundle initially.)  They are tiny (less than 2" x 2") and can be put just about anywhere.  I have mine on the wall with regular push pins.  Ecobee says you should get ~4 years of life out of each battery (worlds better than the 4 or 5 months I get from some of my other smart home accessories), and the range is acceptable but not fantastic.Installation was easy.  I have an older house (late 70s construction) so I only had 4 wires.  The Ecobee requires 5 wires, but comes with an adapter for houses with only 4.  Installation of this adapter requires you to remove the panel on the front of your air handler.  I didnt want to be using a custom adapter, so I bought a spool of 6-wire thermostat cable and ran new cable from my air handler to my thermostat.  Ive seen good results from people that use the adapter, though.  Side comparison: the Nest does not require 5 wires, but does recommend it.  It can theoretically run off of 4 wires, but simply charges an onboard battery any time the air handler is running.  If the battery starts getting low, it will actually run your air handler more than needed to recharge itself!  I much prefer Ecobees honest approach to an adapter than Nests unnecessary additional runtime.  Air handlers use about 500w of electricity simply running the fan!  Not very green, Nest!The primary thermostat is easy to use, though to be honest I almost never touch it.  The interface is mostly intuitive and easy to navigate.  I wish there was a little more customization available for what information shows in idle mode (it changes modes when you approach the thermostat), but right now it displays the current calculated temperature (based on remote sensors that detect motion and the thermostat) as well as the outside weather conditions.Another enjoyable feature: Home IQ.  Having an older home, Im always curious to know how my homes efficiency compares to that of houses around me.  Ecobees Home IQ feature provides you insight into how your house compares to similar houses in your area.  In addition, it tallies total daily runtime, presence sensor activity and temperature history, and a few other things.  If their built-in analytics arent enough, you can download the raw data via .csv.The App works well, and mirrors the interface you are provided on the front of the thermostat.  I do not have any Apple products, but the HomeKit/Siri integration is convenient for those in the Apple ecosystem.  With how rarely I touch my thermostat, I dont mind breaking my phone out or walking to the unit.Overall, I think I made the right choice.  Heres a TL:DRPros:-Saves money quickly over a non-scheduled thermostat-Keeps your house comfortable even if you dont frequent the room containing the thermostat-Provides easy access via an app, web portal, or Siri-Gives you insight into your energy use and system cycle times via their Home IQ portal-Warns you of dangerous or unexpected temperatures inside your house-Active development by Ecobee means constant new features added to the software of the device.Cons:-Sensors are still a little expensive (Id love to see a $20 price point) and can have a limited range-You may need to do a little additional install work if your home has less than 5 wires running to the thermostat

The interior is metallic. Of course if you cut the envelope with scissors it will break but if you try to tear it, it will be a bit hard or impossible. (Probably my favorite I've found.)- Leaves spaces to incorporate your own doodles and details in.  (Not something I wanted, but some people might.)- Images aren't too repetitive of each other but do follow a common style.- Good size of book.  I have some larger ones that are beautiful (Color Me 2 and 4), but they're so big it's harder to work with them in a small space and even harder to turn them around to get at different angles for coloring different things.  This one fit easily onto my desk and I was able to rotate it around as I colored without having to take the page out.- Nice, thick paper with a very slight texture.  I used Staedtler Triplus Fineliners and Stabilo 88 pens and have enjoyed using both in this book.  The darker Staedtler colors will show through just faintly, though, so you may have to stick to only coloring one side of the page.Cons:- Tiny, TINY spaces to color.  Lots of detail is great, but some pictures are made up of such small spaces it will be difficult to use colored pencil.  It might work if you keep your pencil super sharp, but then you're going to wear down the pencil much faster.  My Prismacolor already tend to break frequently so I avoid sharpening more than I have to.  Nothing is worse than wearing down expensive supplies in a hurry.  However, I love this book SO much and have found out how much I enjoy using the fineliner pens with it.  I've also picked up a couple other pencil brands to try to see if I can find something that will work better for this as well as my other books.- Pages are printed front and back.  If you're using anything that bleeds through, this means you're going to have to pick which side of each page you want to forfeit.  If this bothers you, there is an "Artist" edition of this book which is only printed on one side of the page.- Images are printed right up to the binding.  This just bothers me because it's much harder to get into those areas to color sometimes, which is frustrating on a pictures that require a lot of coloring near the binding.

This is a nice book to color, but I will offer a tip on the coloring books out there in general.Most are NOT printed on heavy, quality, acid free paper. If you want a beautiful artwork you can frame, I suggest a copy of the chosen line art onto quality heavy (100lb or more) paper that will take all media. Using artist grade quality pencils, pens where the colors are mostly lightfast will also not only produce the lovely, rich colors, but they will not fade over time. The pages can be loosely stored in a folder, rather than bound and the original coloring book will be kept clean, ready to copy onto decent paper. The copies can be enlarged or reduced to suit your needs :)Also Prismacolor is a wax based colored pencil. Great colors, but not all are lightfast and the colors can get a waxy bloom if several layers are applied. The colored pages need to be sprayed and sealed to prevent this. Polychromos pencils like Faber-Castel are oil based and don't have that issue and most are light fast. It's fun to play with a mix of media like pencils, inks, gel pens and experiment.

reviewText: Love the Echo Dot. I got the buy 3 discount, which makes it worth while. I got it mostly for my 93 year old mother whom I take care of, as she constantly asks me what day or time it is, so now she can ask the Echo. I also like the ability to get a weather report for the day, and I still need to set up the calendar for daily events for mom, once I get that set up it will be another great advantage in having this. I hope they can come up with a way to make this an intercom also between rooms so that if she needs me at any time Echo can alert me in some way. That alone would make this a really great item worth five stars.  So far my favorite feature is the radio, I just ask it to play a particular type of music and it comes on. You do have to be specific about how to get the type of music you want to hear rather than just ask it to play a particular genre. I also like that you can vocally tell it to turn down or up the volume, and to skip the song playing and it goes to the next one. I don't use it to shop with, might be helpful to some. Also, it does take a little adjusting to the way some people speak, my voice is clear but moms is a little muffles so it took a few times of asking questions to get it use to her voice, now it works good for her. The distance to where it can hear you is good and volume on answering and music is great, you don't really need added speakers unless you want to hear it over a very large room, or whole house.Pros: Received quickly with free Prime shipping, ability to play music, ask for date, time, and weather without touching anything, get answeres to a lot of questions, and the ability to update and improve over time. I'm going to be completely honest: I was totally unimpressed with this brush as I was using it.My typical routine is wash > dry > straighten > curl. Yes, I have to straighten before I curl or else it is a frizzy mess. My hair is somewhat thin, but very frizzy - so it looks thick. It is also very long now, almost to my lower back, and dyed. With my current routine I would only need to separate my hair once, and i'd straighten then curl the bottom, then the top. I also have the type of hair that curling irons and hot rollers WILL NOT work on at all - the only thing that will wave/curl my hair is a straighter used as a curler, and a very hot curling *wand*.So with this brush, I left my hair up in a towel for a while then blow dried for about 3 minutes to 95% dry or so. I ended up misting because I think that was a bit too dry. I then sectioned into 3 parts, bottom-middle-very top, and began using the brush. As I said, I was very unimpressed and actually annoyed while using it because it didn't seem like it was doing ANYTHING. It was drying, but it didn't look like anything special. I proceeded anyway, just to be fair.And well, when I let all the layers down and did the magical hair flip/finger comb, it came together and I was very surprised! It looked wonderful! The frizz level was acceptable, it was smooth and shiny, and I definitely had tons more volume than usual (actually was kind of weird as I never really went for volume before). There was the slight wave you get from a blow out. The style looks much different from my current routine, which is what I wanted: something different. I'm very happy with the results, especially for the price of the brush.I have very long hair, and also *no* layers, as my hair is just too thin - they don't work right in my hair. If you have layers/shorter hair, I think you're going to like it even more. My "bangs" (I don't really have bangs, but that part of my hair is shorter), look the best they ever have - and I attribute it to this brush & that part of my hair being shorter.Another thing I liked is that even on the hottest setting, it would not burn me. I could wrap my hand around the barrel thanks to the long bristles to hold the hair in place as I positioned it. Not once did I even come close to burning myself. It sounds like a hairdryer, but much quieter. Because of the gentle heat, I felt that I was doing less damage then with my straightener set to 450 degrees.

From the beginning we are dropped into the world of which magic and belief are interwoven. And while the two are interwoven, magic is viewed with fear and those that practice it, or more likely are born with it, are locked away under the care and protection of trained guards called, Sentinels. Looking over that sentence again, I think it is more apt to say that "care and protection" leans more towards imprisonment than care. The world does need those magic users, those Mages, and they are brought out, under the guarding of a team of Sentinels when their services are needed.This is where our story begins, with the transferring of a Mage to another city. Kalinda, or Kali as you will get to know her, is a Mage that was born with a defect that can be healed by another Mage in another city. Having learned that, she requested a transfer, leaving everything she knew before behind. While the routine travel is underway the troupe is attacked by Calandri, a foe that while quite fierce generally has suddenly acquired demonic elements and the group of Sentinel are overtaken. Only by chance do Kalinda and a Sentinel named Stonewall get away.The rest of the book covers their travels toward their original destination, Whitewater, as well as the unrest of relationships between a few Sentinels and Mages already there.This book is the beginning to a much longer series (I hope). It leaves you with a lot of unresolved questions, but they are questions that you care enough about that you want to read whatever comes next to know the resolution. How do these characters all connect? What really is happening outside of the safe city walls?The character development is great-the book does jump from perspective to perspective a lot and that takes a bit to get used to, though in the end, you have been introduced to quite a few characters and they are all believable. Something that I wonder, though, is what happened to make everyone so weary of mages. If they have been used simply as healers in the past what caused the fear? Will that be something that is brought up in the next book?I look forward to the next installment, I want to find out what happens with Kalinda and Stonewall as they transition into a new season of life in Whitewater. I also need to know how Commander Talon will handle the oncoming attacks from an old foe with new tricks.I received a free copy of Catalyst Moon from the publisher in exchange for a review.

They say that the mark of a good book was if it allowed you to step into another world. This book did this for me with ease. I was carried away. New and unknown things were going on, both with the magic user, commonly called a moonblood in a derogatory way, as well as with the world around them as a new and very dangerous threat begins to show itself - and it's spreading. How it all fits together is a mystery I will happily look into. Kudos to this writer for providing a story so griping as to pull me away from the real world.

One of the most vital aspects that contribute to the success of a fantasy novel is the creation of the world and its internal consistency. It matters not how utterly foreign something that happens in the world, as long as it follows the rules set up by the author. I have, unfortunately, read numerous fantasy novels that have fallen flat because the action of the plot did not follow the rules. This is definitely not the case in this novel. Lauren L. Garcia has crafted a world for us that is filled with magic and with faith. There are rules that govern magic and, even when the magic users don't fully understand how their magic works, the reader is not left feeling like the author simply used that as an excuse to not explain. What I found most fascinating about the book is the fundamental human distrust of anyone who is "different". In this world, mages are so distrusted, so maligned that they are bound with a mineral that dampens their connection to their magic. Even a Mage like Kalinda Halycon, who is voluntarily being transferred is shackled by hematite cuffs and shadowed by a Sentinel. I particularly enjoyed watching Kali and Stonewall start at opposite ends of a spectrum where Kali is ruled by magic, not having need of the gods, and Stonewall living by faith, honor, and duty. As the story progresses, and the pair meet more and more obstacles, they realize that they have both been suffering from numerous misconceptions.In addition to a well-crafted world, the author has created fully-developed secondary characters in a genre where secondary characters are more likely to be stereotypes and caricatures rather than well thought-out, fully-distinguishable characters. I look forward to reading more in this series so I can find out whether Kali and Stonewall are able to pursue the friendship that began on their arduous journey. I also want to learn more about some of the secondary characters like the twins, Milo and Mira.There are some allusions to sex, but there is nothing more explicit than heavy petting in this installment. Also, while the book ends in such a way as to indicate there will likely be future books in the series, it is not a cliffhanger ending, which I definitely appreciate. I very rarely give 5-star reviews, so we'll done, indeed.Reviewed by HR Duby for Romance Authors that Rock

reviewText: When I ordered this item, I saw nothing but glowing reviews...so I did. I had it sent to an address in the US since I live overseas (outside the US). Amazingly, after I ordered it, I started seeing negative reviews. I was VERY worried as I planned to bring it back with me here (to Sweden) after going home for a visit. Once back here, I started using it. It was amazing - no sticking at all, easy clean up, etc. However, something changed...and I had no idea why. I wasn't doing anything differently but things were sticking and BADLY. I was so frustrated having carried these in my luggage (this textured pan as well as the smooth wok). I got on here and started reading some of the comments. I felt I had tried everything - letting it sit overnight with water in it, heating the water, etc. I happened to see a comment by one guy who said salt is a chef's best friend/secret; it's abrasive enough to clean but not too abrasive (so it doesn't scratch). It was a last ditch effort before I threw the pan out the window (I was THAT frustrated). I got an old toothbrush (soft), poured some salt on the pan, and got to cleaning. I was shocked. The stuff that had been stuck on (and would only come off if I scratched it with my finger nail) came off. Once cleaned, it performed pretty much as usual (no problems). Now, of course, I have to use the salt all the time. I don't think this should be necessary but...it is, so I do it. The alternative is to lose the pan. After this situation, I decided to try the wok (up until that time I had not used it). Like the other pan, it has performed great. Will this change soon? I'm not sure but I don't think so. I think the smooth bottom is MUCH better than the textured one. In my case, I chose one smooth and one textured because I wasn't sure which was better. The wok has a smaller bottom area so I can't cook as much but...it's less trouble. One important thing to note (and others have mentioned it as well), the heat shouldn't be too high. We have an induction stove so perhaps it's even more important with these (I'm not sure).Bottom line - I like these pans but...I wouldn't buy another textured bottom pan. My husband asked why they had it. I told him it had something to do with airflow. I would argue that, while perhaps it's a good idea in theory, it doesn't work in practice. As of now, I really like the smooth bottom wok, so I would consider buying another one of those. That said, there may be better pans out there but this was reasonably priced and performs pretty well...though cleaning is more cumbersome.Hope this helps someone!
reviewTitle: Using salt to clean is the key!

reviewText: Have to say I was surprised. It works! This kept popping up on my FB page. Found it on Amazon and I'm so glad I ordered it. It's easy and not any more painful than tweezing or waxing.

I bought this to try out as a replacement for waxing at home with an electric warming pot and muslin strips. The coil is all you need to remove hair, and eliminates the mess and time that comes with waxing. I like that I can do this while watching TV, reading, etc, and there is virtually no clean up involved. The only drawbacks I found with it is that you can ONLY use the coil for lip/chin/cheek areas, and NOT on eyebrows, legs, etc, and that it does take a little bit longer than waxing to get to end result. I have pretty fine facial hair, and it took me multiple passes over an area to completely remove hair (about 20 minutes from start to finish). The benefit with this, however, is that you can go over an area as many times as you want without pulling or tearing skin, which is a risk with waxing the same area of skin over and over.I have fair, sensitive skin, and was worried that this would cause swelling or severe redness, but was excited when neither happened. The coil is painful to use at first (I thought slightly more so than waxing), but after a few uses, my skin got used the process and hurt much less. I have not had any ingrown hairs or breakouts from using this product, which was an added bonus. The directions to say to clean/disinfect the skin to be treated before and after, but I've forgotten to do this a few times and haven't noticed any negative effects. For $15, this tool pays for itself if you get regular waxes or buy depilatory kits, and doesn't seem to have the cons that some other methods do (stinging, smell, cleanup, skin darkening, etc.)

reviewText: ----First 24 hours---- will update again in a couple of days-----( feel free to skip to the 2nd P)I had an MPOW Shift before I purchased the BTS+.It was my first wireless headphone, which I really loved the first 2 days before it died...completely. It's a $30  headphones,and it sure feel and perform as one (maybe even worse). I don't wanna spend much money on it since the only time I use it is in the gym, yet I don't want to get another lemon. So I decided to splurge up a bit since I saw this brand on CNET's best wireless headphones for under $100. Upon reading the reviews here in Amazon and YouTube - I'm sold!My initial impression as I was excitedly unboxing this headphone was, wow this seems like a superior quality product  and boy was I right!The box felt solid when I held it and the contents was packaged nicely overall.It comes with a nice and sturdy set of 3' micro USB charging cable. Seriously, this cable feels more superior than the one my Zenfone 2 came with.Inside the box you will find a couple of small packets/manuals, which you most likely won't need.I unwrapped the headset and to my surprise, it's not as big as it looks on the pictures.I was expecting it to cover my entire ears, but I can actually see my earrings even with it on. (I do have an enormous head and ear, I must admit).I mustered up some patience and fully charged the headset first before using it.Connecting it was as easy as 1-2-3. No issues at all.I immediately opened Pandora began listening some heavy dubstep, and I must say.. I was blown away!I won't consider myself a headset connoisseur or an expert when it comes to music products, but I do know how to appreciate a good sound quality!This headset did not disappoint at all! The base was almost as good as my Skullcandy Crusher, but the overall sound and clarity is actually better.I used it while driving to the gym. They sit perfectly on my ears. However, you need to find an angle that's comfortable for you. The actual loop that goes over the ear bothered me a bit the first time, I even felt some pain. I quickly re-positioned the band and I didn't have problems since then. I even did jump ropes and it didn't come off or anything. However, one thing to point out is that it may move slightly when you're laying on your head (e.g. during benchpress) due to the band that goes around your neck. Not so much to where the cuffs would go off the ears.Regarding the looks and feel: when I looked in the mirror it's actually pretty bulky on the side. The LED on the right cuff also blinks every after 20sec or so. I'm not a big fan of it. It looked kinda awkward, but I try not to really care much when I'm in the gym. You might also read some comments about the control buttons being too big and clicky. The buttons are located on the right cuff. Its quite massive and honestly, I'm still not quite used to them. You will definitely hear the buttons when being pressed. To some people this may be annoying, but I didn't let that sway me from writing a positive review.One actual problem I encountered is that, it sometimes get "cut off" for a brief half a second or so. As this doesn't bother me as much, I know some people can be very critical about stuff like this. I will update this in a couple of days if the problem persists. I also noticed that it has a much shorter connectivity range. I'd say you'd slowly start dropping signal after 15ft.But what really impressed me is the mic and voice quality! Like I've said, I planned on using this solely for workingout, but I still get calls even when I'm in the gym. Sometimes I answer them,sometimes I don't. Part of the reason I don't answer calls in the gym (besides the obvious) is that I ALWAYS have to either remove the headphones I'm using or place the mic closer to my mouth otherwise they won't be able to hear me. I've tried many,many headphones before, they all had the same issue when accepting calls especially on a loud environment.I liked it so much that I find myself listening to it on the way home with my car radio off and the windows rolled down. This proves that the noise cancelling mic actually works. You don't usually find that on "cheap" products like this. Sweat-proof, 20+ hours of battery, superior sound and build quality, fast charging, etc, are claims you don't actually expect to get in reality when purchasing a $50 headphone, but you get all that with this!Overall, this is by far the BEST budget bluetooth headphones you can buy for under $50...arguably even $100!I rate it 4.7 stars. This could easily be a 5 star if:1. They improve the connectivity and range a little bit2. They care enough to maybe put a soft and comfortable rubber lining along the loop that goes on top of the ear to make it more comfortable.3. Better button layout ergonomics (I did not take off points because of this).

This story made me laugh, cry, my heart pound and if I were a nail biter I would have been chewing on them. Do yourself a favor and read this exciting book. I have already told my husband that he will thoroughly enjoy it also.

Jake Wolfe is a photojournalist trailing a criminal lawyer in the hope of getting a story, but he gets more than he bargains for when he witnesses a murder and becomes a target of assassin Ivan Zhukov. Also known as The Artist for his creative and artistic kills, Ivan has been contracted by a mysterious international organization to kill several lawyers. But what is their real agenda? Will Jake be able to stop him in time?While the story is good, the book is overly long and needs a severe edit. Problems include: too many physical descriptions of characters; irrelevant scenes, information, and conversations; constant over-explaining; unnecessary translations of basic phrases; numerous editing errors, including punctuation and poorly phrased sentences; back story told as dialogue; reports that read as narratives; unbelievable dialogue; multiple viewpoints, even those of the dogs, sometimes from paragraph to paragraph; too many coincidences, e.g., everybody seems to know everybody and they keep bumping into each other even though the action takes place in San Francisco; questionable character behaviors, e.g., Jake gets out of a long-term relationship and immediately sleeps with one woman and lusts over at least two more, and Ivan is always talking to himself and (conveniently) letting us know what's happening.That being said, the story maintained my interest to the end. A nice touch is the way that music features throughout, with particular songs setting the tone for different scenes. Despite its flaws, this is still a good read for those looking for non-stop action, interesting characters, a touch of humor, and a bit of romance.

I have long, wavy, somewhat thin hair which was fully dried, product-free, brushed out, and tangle-free when I tested out the Miraqueen Professional Curling Iron.  My hair consistently got tangled in the curling chamber.  I turned off the device each time to keep my hair from getting damaged by the heat and it took several minutes for each attempt to release my hair from the chamber.  If my hair ever got stuck to the point that I couldn't remove it (which didn't happen), I was fully prepared to break the device before ever considering chopping off a section of hair.  So- why keep trying to curl my hair if it kept getting stuck?  I wanted to make sure it wasn't user error.  (Plus- I wanted to make sure I'd have a thoroughly written product review.)  I tried smaller sections of hair, larger sections of hair, and in-between.  I tried both the 370* and 410* temperate settings.  I also tried straitening my hair, and then curling it again, which didn't help either.  Sometimes, the device only partly took my hair and didn't suck the ends into the chamber.  There were multiple times when, after sucking up the middle and end sections of hair, the device sucked itself against my scalp.  It didn't burn, but it certainly hurt because it was trying to pull my hair out of my head.  During the few times that the device actually seemed to work, (when it sucked up the whole section of hair without sucking itself to my scalp and it properly released the curl) the curls came out terrible.  I feel like this was due to the fact that, after sucking up the end section of hair, it kept trying to suck up more and more hair that wasn't there, which could have tightly curled some of the hair in the chamber.  What I'm trying to say is that- the area that I clamped the device down on, came out crimped.  The section of hair right below that came out tightly curled (curls the size of your thumb).  I was using the 8 second time setting which should have resulted in a loose curl.  The end section of hair was the only part that came out looking perfect.  Again, I'll point out- there were Very Few times that the chamber actually released my hair.  This curling iron hurt my head, possibly damaged my hair a bit, pulled out many strands of hair, could have left me with the decision to either break the device or cut my hair, and the resulting curls were disastrous looking.  It was a huge pain in the butt and I will be returning it.  I'm sure it's a great curling iron for most chicks, however, I think long, thin haired women should avoid this product.

I had been eyeing the MiraCurl for a few years now but couldn't justify the price.  My husband ended up getting me this for Christmas and I'm so glad he did.  I love it!!!  I have been using it every other day since then and feel I have enough experience with it now to finally post my review (although I wanted to gush about it right away!)I have very fine, unprocessed, medium length hair (about 2-3 inches past my shoulders) that has never held a curl a day in my life until now.  Because of my fine hair, I have only ever used this on the lowest heat and curl time setting (370 degrees/8 seconds) so my review is for that heat and time setting only.  The machine itself takes about 1 minute from the time you turn it on until it's ready to use at this setting. You will know it's ready when it stops blinking and you hear three rapid beeps. You can curl your hair to the left, right or auto (which alternates between the two). I find it works best when you put 1-1.5 inches of hair in the curler at a time.  Any more than that seems to get caught, which has happened to me, but infrequently.  When it does, it's always my fault from putting too much hair in at once and the machine promptly stops.  My hair has never gotten tangled or stuck; it slides out easily.Even at the lowest setting, I cannot believe how curly this makes my hair.  You can get the barrel quite close to your head too so it curls from root to tip.  I've used it on both freshly washed and unwashed hair and it works beautifully either way.  This seriously leaves my entire head with full, voluminous, bouncy curls!!  I prefer softer waves so I just run my fingers through it a few times after I'm done and I'm good to go.  Since I wash my hair every other day, I can say that the curls last until my next wash so, for 48 hours. No, they're not as tight as when I first use it, but that's also because I run my fingers through them to soften them up.  The machine is so easy to use too and on average, I have timed the entire process at 14 minutes to do my whole head.  You can't beat it!!  I love this machine and can't say enough good things about it.  It's awesome and truly works.***** UPDATE (2/1/16) *****It has been well over a year since I first started using this and it still works great!!  I still love it and it has held up under near constant use (just about every other day).  I even dropped the thing once from my bathroom vanity and it's still working great.  I will say that every now and then I do have to re-curl a strand of hair that did not curl the first time, but it's not a big deal.  It's probably because of build up on the barrel which I guess is expected over time.  I see that Amazon has not been selling this anymore for a while so I'm hoping the one I have will last forever.  I can't live without it!!! :)

reviewText: I had rabbit fur absolutely matted into a rug. I hadn't figured out how to get rid of it -- and it had been building up for over a year. Finally I got this and it works wonders! I have to say, it takes a fair amount of elbow grease to lift that fur out of the rug (probably easier in a longer fiber carpet than a dense area rug), but it really does work. You *must* use the hard attachment first to get rid of any debris, and *then* you can switch to the rubber attachment to aggressively push/pull the fur out of your carpet or rug. If you don't do that, then the exhaust fan will indeed blow debris all over (this is a complaint from other reviewers). The reason (I think) that the exhaust is so powerful is because the suction of the vacuum is so powerful. Really, it's very intense! But that powerful suction, plus the rubber with the nubs to push/pull at the fur that is embedded in your carpet/rug is what actually does the trick and why a traditional vacuum is practically useless! I would also add that the price is unbelievable. I was thinking of paying more for the cordless, and, yes, corded can be a bit annoying (but it's a very long cord, which is great), but frankly, it takes a long time to really get that fur out of the carpet, so a cordless would probably die before I am done. (After I get a year's worth of fur out of my area rug, then it should not take nearly as long to do regular vacuuming!) Anyway, great purchase. Well worth the minimal cost. Highly recommend.

It's difficult for me to find chelated magnesium in quantity locally. I am taking vitamin d supplements, and I have learned that vitamin d alone without additional magnesium caused me to have heart palpitations. By experiment, I have learned that I need to take 600 mg of magnesium a day, which means I take six of these tablets spread throughout the day. My local Costco sells 400 mg magnesium tablets, but it is in the form of magnesium oxide, which did nothing to help my palpitations. I have read that the body does not readily absorb the magnesium from magnesium oxide tablets.My local Target does sell chelated magnesium, but in small quantities, which would make buying 600 mg doses there expensive. I am not a chemist, so I can not definitively comment on the quality of these tablets. All I can say is that they work whereas the magnesium oxide tablets sold locally do not, and the price is right.A word of caution, if you buy magnesium supplements and the label says only "magnesium," the tablets are almost certainly low-quality magnesium oxide.

Handy little device. When the usb port stopped working on my daughter's Nexus 7 tablet, I picked this up to verify it was the port and not the battery or some other problem keeping it from powering on. Sure enough, the tablet charged up sitting on this.I can, however, see why wireless charging isn't all the rage. From 0-100% charge on the Nexus 7 took between 5 and 6 hours. I had similar results with my Nexus 5 phone. Smaller battery, so a little faster to recharge, but still a very lengthy amount of time vs a full charge in around 1 hour via the usb cable.As long as you have a decent power supply, this pad attaches to the device pretty easily and reliably, even through a case. The first USB adapter I tried the light flickered even with nothing on it, and it wouldn't attach (green light) easily. Obviously that cheap USB power adapter has some problems. I switched to a computer USB and got good results, then switched to my Nexus 5 adapter and it worked just as well, though charging was just as slow. Also tried charging both devices without a case on, thinking closer proximity might speed it up, but with no noticeable improvement.So, this is handy if you leave it by the bed and drop your phone on it overnight. Plenty of time to charge. Of course, plugging it in overnight isn't difficult, and either method you need a usb power source nearby. Might be handy for keeping on your desk and keeping your device topped up during the day. Easy to pick up and use for a few minutes, then set back down and get back to charging. Though, I have no idea whether that little trickle charge here and there has any adverse effects on long term battery health.

This is a very effective little antenna, especially for the price. I live in Queens, New York City, in an apartment with no unobstructed view towards the local broadcast towers, and this pulls in a couple dozen channels including a few from New Jersey.However, I want to emphasize that this is a LITTLE antenna. The 'ears' are quite short and can't be positioned horizontally - they only swivel out to a 45 degree angle. This limits its effectiveness. For a few bucks more, the Philips SDV1125T/27 Indoor HDTV/UHF/VHF/FM Antenna installed in the same spot gets at least two channels clearly that are garbled and unwatchable with this RCA.Edit: I found I could beef up this antenna by attaching a wire clothes hanger to it, which now brings in the two stations I mentioned above. That's a big advantage for rabbit ear antennas! On the other hand, one of the 'ears' bent and almost broke while I was fiddling with it - they're pretty flimsy.

I don't know the range of this antenna but after cutting the cord and checking tvfool.com, I determined I live within 9 miles of all major network TV stations in Jax,FL.  It took maybe 5 minutes to set up on top of the entertainment center and a little longer to scan channels.  Go to tvfool.com to find out station locations and signal strength in relation to your address.  Anyway, like magic, HDTV. Some stations are more defined than others, 480p vs 1080p for example.  Hey for the price and old school appeal, rabbit ears : ), this little passive receptor is a bargain.Since the last review, I've had signal troubles with some stations, especially PBS.  I decided to take the antenna outside and connect it directly to the coaxial cable.  I set the antenna on the adjacent electric meter box and now I get 23 stations most over 75% signal strength.

We've been using various Roku products for years. There was a time when we were so impressed with the Roku we'd buy them as gifts for friends. They tend to be fairly reliable and for the most part have a simple to use interface. However, I've noticed changes with the newer models changes which are diminishing my affection for these products.Let me begin by explaining how we use the Roku. Perhaps 60% of the time, we use it to stream content. Netflix, Amazon, Vimeo, YouTube,etc. The remainder of the time, it is used for content stored on a 2 TB WD USB Passport Drive. Most of the content played from the USB drive is music. The older Roku were ideal for this as they offered RCA AV ports which could easily be plugged into a stereo. This new model however no longer has this feature. It's too bad, as this was a great way to play an endless supply of music we like without commercials. With the new Roku, you need to patch your music through your TV and then route it to a stereo. A big waste of electricity.Another problem introduced by Roku relative to music is that the old version of the media player was able to recursively search folders and randomize play across all those folders. Now it will only randomize within a single folder. They also altered the player so it lists song by other than the file name, as a result you can't play an entire album in its original order any longer.  When I queried the support people at roku and asked how to get back to what it was they simply told me tough luck. When I asked if I could go back to the original version I was basically told go screw myself. Which brings me to another problem I have with the Roku. You are at the mercy of their idiot designers and required updates.If roku decides they want to change the way your roku works, they go right ahead and do it without asking. If you don't like what they've changed, tough crap on you. This is an alarming trend among many tech providers, they treat your property likes it's really their property and you're lucky they let you use it at all. More and more tech devices have basically become sales showrooms you have to pay to walk into. Can you imagine being charged to walk into a department store? It sure seems like a great many tech company believe you should.This brings me to a pet peeve, Roku likes to change your theme around for different holidays and events. They go into your Roku and change what they like. Seems to me you bought it, you should be able to set it up any way your chose. Clearly changing themes has nothing to do with the operation of the unit so where do they come off invading your space?Which comes to another pet peeve. I went with a Roku to get away from advertising. I bought my own hardware and pay a subscription, but guess what I see taking up a greater and great proportion of my menu screen. I've also noted there seems to be many more commercials invading my TuneIn and YouTube sessions. Another alarming trend. It's like showing up on time at the movie theater and being forced to watch a dozen movie trailers before they show the film you are actually paying to see. Why are you playing for no commercials only to get .... commercials.But I'm also becoming more and more concerned about privacy on the roku. I'm beginning to wonder what information Roku and the various services are collecting as this device is used. I know I can go on Netflix and see a complete list of basically everything I've ever watched. Why is such personal information be collected and how is it being used against me and my wishes? In general, consumers are allowing too many companies to invade their devices. They are giving away information about themselves and companies are using that information to fill their coffers at the expense of the very individuals they are alleged to be serving. Why doesn't this bother everyone? Companies are using your personal information to earn all kinds of money. When was the last time they sent you a commission check, I mean after all; it is your information they're using and selling. Do you think they're going to pay for the milk when you're willingly giving it away for free?As a streaming device, the Roku is probably the best of the current available choices. There is a fairly robust selection of "channels" there is also a catalog of "private" channels to which you may gain access. In this regard the device is useful. I will however say, that I believe recent changes to the Roku software seem to great favor advertisers and seem to make it easier for content providers to impose advertising into content as you watch. I'm not happy about this apparent changes.For all these reasons and a few more not mentioned, Roku has converted us from a family who loved the product so much we'd buy them to give as gifts; to a family who is looking elsewhere for a better alternative.

Spirulina is a blue-green algae that forms in freshwater lakes in consistently warm environments, this one is grown in California. It is a cyanobacterium which consists of two species of bacteria: Arthrospira platensis, which is native to Africa, Asia and South America and Arthrospira maxima which comes from Central America. This comes with 180 tablet and you can take 6 pills in one serving, I like to take all 6 at once with my lunch. Spirulina is considered both a dietary supplement and a health food. It was also consumed by both the Aztecs and Mesoamericans up to the 16th century in the Mexico region, but was rediscovered in the 1960s and has been growing in popularity ever since. There is no wonder why too because this truly is an amazing superfood, I feel great since I have been taking these. Spirulina contains up to 5 times more protein than meat, and contains as many as 100 different nutrients including many vitamins, potassium, copper, iron, selenium, zinc and magnesium. All of the extra protein is helping my hair and fingernails grow. It is one of the few products that contains all the essential amino acids, as well as five times more beta-carotene than carrots. As a plant protein is has smaller amounts of methionine, cysteine and lysine than meat, but the levels are still higher than other plant protein. I love this supplement and I will continue to take this in the future and if you want to be healthy I suggest you do the same.

reviewText: When I was researching buying these I looked at the remote shown on Amazon's website and thought it looked cheap and would probably be the weak point in the durability of these devices. To my surprise the ones I received have a more modern and attractive design as well as looking and feeling sturdier. (I submitted a picture which you should be able to see here on the website)I really like these as they are very useful for lights or other electronics that are plugged in in hard to reach areas.  A battery for the remote is included. The replacement battery is an A23 Battery, 12 Volt like the Energizer A23 Battery, 12 Volt - 2 Pack. For in home use I usually stick these to a wall with Velcro sticky back tape; this way you don't lose the remotes but you can easily pull them off the wall if you need to.There is only one 3 prong outlet to plug things into. In order to get around the channel limitation I have paired this with a Ziotek ZT1120131 HC1 Black Liberator Dual Outlet Wall Adapter, 2 Pack. I think I'll be trying the Leviton 692-W 15 Amp, 125 Volt, Triple Cube Grounding Adapter, White for my next bright idea. Not sure how these adapter would work outside as so far I am using them in either the house or garage.I ordered 4 of these and each one is a different channel. They sell these in 6 different channels (A-F). You cannot change the channel. The ones I received are channels A, C, D, & F. What this means is that if I had 2 different lamps in the same room and I wanted to turn them both on or off at the same time I would need to press the on/off button on both remotes. I had hoped that at least two of them would be the same channel but you can't specify what channels you want when you order. I hope that Woods will provide that option in the future.When you press the "on" button of the remote it turns on the light (or whatever you have plugged into it) and also turns on a small but bright red light on the plugged in connector unit. This doesn't matter much if it's outside or plugged in behind a couch but if it is someplace that is visible the light is rather glaring. For example, I gave one to my Mom to turn on a lamp that is in the front window. The wall plug is behind some sheer curtains and the light on it shines brightly through the curtains and is unsightly. A problem like this is really minor as a piece of duck tape over the light easily solves the problem.I am currently using a Skylink WS-100/WS-100N Wireless Remote Control, Channel A for a bedroom lamp and while they are very reliable they are also quite expensive. These are much more reasonably priced at about $8 when I bought them. These exact Woods units sell for $17.99 at Home Depot.So far these are working well but I'm giving this just 4 stars for now until I further test the distance these work from, how well they work outside, whether the remote holds up and if the "signal travels through walls, windows and doors" as the manufacturer claims. I would like to be able to use it to turn on a fan in the basement from upstairs . . . we'll see how that goes. I will update my review after I've had these a while longer.

reviewText: Difficult to button up after you fill the cards

This is one of those products that I've gotten suckered into based on unrealistically over-the-top reviews.  Why do I fall for that?  I should have known better.  At best, this is an okay business card holder, but make no mistake---this is not a great item, and certainly not a substitute for a real wallet.  And as far as business card holders go, it's bulky, and fairly cheap looking.  And it lacks personality.  I think I'm being generous by giving it 3 stars---it's okay, I guess, but I don't actually see myself wanting to use this on a daily basis.There are several big problems from my perspective:1.)  The cover is one continuous piece of thick leather.  There are no seams or cuts hat would make the cover fold easier or lay flatter, like a booklet.  Instead, it wants to form a loose cylinder, unless you really flatten it with your hand.  It's much too cumbersome to stuff in your pocket, and frankly, it's too cumbersome for my backpack or work bag as well.2.)  The leather is so bulky that a single center snap doesn't do much to corral everything nicely.  The material on either side of the flap just wings upward unattractively.3.)  The two metal tips on the corners seem like an afterthought.  They don't serve much of a purpose, and they just emphasize how badly the cover closes.I'm sorry, but this looks like a cheaply made dollar store find,  and I have a hard time understanding the rave reviews.  The quality is shoddy, and the poorly designed bulk not only makes it impractical, but also unenjoyable to carry.This is not the card case for me, I'm afraid.  It's not a pleasure to carry, and not a luxurious item.  I'd hate to give business contacts my card from a card holder like this.---Promotional sample provided for the purpose of evaluation and objective review.---

reviewText: I'll admit, when I first started reading The Sorcery Code, I thought it was going to be one of those cheesy sci-fi fantasy love stories and immediately rolled my eyes. NOT AT ALL! I loved this book and can't wait to get into the next one! Yes, I'll admit, it does have some of that cheese in it, but for the most part it's a great story, with quite a few twists and turns in the plot. I love each of the characters and haven't decided which one is my favorite, they all are pretty awesome in their own right. A great read, all in all. **I did receive this book from the author through Tomoson for an honest review.**

At first when I started reading this story it was a bit confusing. It keep going back and forth between Blaise and then to Augusta and Barson. It almost seems like I was reading two different stories.I liked Blaise because he was all for helping the commoners. He was the good guy. Then he created Gala and what was not to love about her. She was so innocent and wanted to learn about the world. Blaise wanted to protect her.Then the what had seemed like two different stories merged and Augusta who was Blaise's ex-fiance was checking up on Blaise to see if he had become an addict.Augusta is riddled with fear of anything that is not exactly how she was brought up. I really don't think I like her very much. But she is really just a 100% by the rules type of person.Gala goes away with 2 of Blaise's commoner friends and tried to experience the world. In doing this she is led by emotion several times to use powers she didn't even realize she had to help people.Of course this exposes her and Barson and his army finds her and there is a climactic battle. I won't tell you how it ends and spoil the story but I will say that I can't wait to read more.My opinion is that it is worth reading and that you will want to read the next book in line as well. I think I like it so much because there is an underlying love story even though noting ever happens.I also liked that is was a good clean story withouth the profanity and adult scenes some books seem to think necessary.Disclosure: I was given this book for free to read and give my honest opinion. I received no compensation. #SorceryCode

I absolutely love Josephine and her friends and foibles. Lots of great stuff is going on in this book. First of all, it's very funny, while at the same time being propelled by a good plot, making for a really engaging read. The humor arises from the biting dialogue, which is really clever, believable, and adds depth to the characters. For example, one character called her ex 'Spot" in reference to his complexion and his doggish behavior, and funny details like that are liberally sprinkled in to the scenes. Josephine is a great character, an aging wizard who just wants to retire. She's fantastic and if she were my aunt I'd be thrilled to visit her in Siesta Key, even though trouble follows her, or rather calls on her, as she is required by the government to assist in the solving of crimes based on her keen abilities to read energy in a room or off of a victim, much like a forensic scientist reads physical evidence. Really cool concept that is well executed throughout.Another strength in the story is the creation of the world of wizards, with all of their powers, limitations, strength and vulnerabilities. O'Riley has done a great job of invoking complex rules of how a world that somewhat accepted these powers would try to use and control them, and having Josephine up against all of that as she tries to solve a serial murder case is excellent. It's all very well done, unfolds visually like a rewarding movie, and readers will be satisfied with the way it crosses many genres.

reviewText: I have heard about Indian Healing Clay for a long time, so when the opportunity to test it out and review it came up, I was excited. Having never used bentonite clay before, I wasn't really sure what to expect or how to use it. The clay itself, as it comes, is a dry gray powder. Following the instructions, I mixed it with some water  and tried to get a good consistency. That's where my inexperience came into play.After mixing, I was left with a still chunky mixture which didn't apply too well. I gradually added more water until I achieved a somewhat usable consistency. Also due to my unfamiliarity with the substance, I made much more than I could use at one time. I did some research online afterwards, and it seems the best method is to make it in bulk, and let it sit for a day or two in order for the clay to absorb all the water. I assume this would give you a better consistency. I have the rest still sitting at home, so I will try again to see if sitting helps out.I can't fault the product for my inexperience, just something you need to learn before you mix it. No big deal. I currently have some sunburn on my face, so it was actually a good time to try this product. After the 20 minutes and cleaning the mask off, my face had a clean, smooth, 'matte' feel to it. I experienced no side effects or irritation and I have somewhat sensitive skin. A lot of the dead skin that had started to peel from the sunburn came off as well.I would definitely recommend this product for anyone looking to improve their complexion and skin. In my research, I found that there are a ton of beneficial uses for bentonite clay and with the amount that comes in this jar, it seems like it would last me a lifetime!
